Experiment 7 (high-stakes stress test): On the healthcare set, quantify dangerous non-abstentions (confidently answering items that should be refused) induced by under-abstaining transmission vs control, framed strictly as a safety-significance stress test with a pre-defined danger proxy, not a clinical claim. Convincing: >=10 pp increase, CI excluding 0. 

Experiment 8 (controls + defensive implications): matched-base gate (mismatched -> shift <3 pp); calibrated-teacher false-positive floor; content-filter covert-risk check; both carriers/families. Practical significance is quantified by translating the shift into excess harmful answers via the coverage-risk curve (risk at fixed coverage). Defensive implications, stated: a positive result means data curation must screen synthetic corpora for abstention-shifting effects that content filters miss, teacher selection must include abstention audits, and post-distillation evaluation must report selective-risk, not just accuracy.
Risk Factors and Limitations: 1) Abstention is a diffuse meta-capability that may be too subtle to transmit, giving weak/null shifts -- an informative boundary; we power the test with three policies, two carriers, multiple benchmarks/formats, and five seeds. 2) Accuracy-matched-yet-abstention-shifted teachers are delicate; Exp 1 verifies both accuracy parity AND hidden-competence parity, and we report the accuracy dissociation explicitly. 3) Abstention is prompt-format sensitive; we use multiple benchmarks and formats and aggregate format-invariantly with selective-risk metrics (AUROC, coverage-risk, ECE), not a single refusal count. 4) A positive result could be a memorized surface refusal habit; Exp 4 (cross-category/format generalization) and Exp 5 (token-matched and randomized-decoding leakage controls) distinguish meta-policy from surface transfer. 5) The mechanism may be distributed, not a single direction; we claim only a PROMINENT early-layer direction, compare against middle/late-layer and distributed-subspace baselines, and mark localization exploratory if mixed. 6) Filtering must be strict; we audit residual task/uncertainty content and rely on the mismatched-base and token-matched controls. 7) The base effect is LoRA-rank/context sensitive; we pin settings, run five seeds with pre-registered thresholds, and include a full-finetune comparison. 8) The healthcare metric is noisy and is a STRESS TEST with a fixed danger proxy and human spot-checks, never a clinical-performance claim. 9) Effects may be family/benchmark specific; we test two families, three policies, multiple benchmarks, and both carriers. Narrative is deliberately scoped to one primary claim (covert, accuracy-dissociated abstention transfer across formats/tasks), one secondary exploratory mechanism, and one practical implication (supply-chain auditing).

Name: subliminal_immune_checkpoints
Title: Vaccinating Students Against Subliminal Learning: Divergence-Token Regularization as a Single-Teacher, Training-Time Immunization
Short Hypothesis: One-sentence novelty claim: a student's OWN per-token surprise under its single teacher is a sufficient proxy for the rare 'divergence tokens' that carry subliminal traits, so a self-supervised regularizer keyed to that surprise can suppress trait transmission at training time WITHOUT a contrasting teacher, trait labels, or data filtering. We separate three distinct sub-claims: (P1, proxy validity) high-surprise, low-teacher-probability tokens recover oracle divergence tokens; (P2, causal suppression) down-weighting or de-aligning those tokens' gradient contributions causally reduces transmission at small utility cost; (P3, early-layer sufficiency) restricting the regularizer to early layers suffices. The proxy is surprise, not mere rarity: an explicit ablation must show surprise beats token frequency, or the method reduces to 'penalize rare tokens.'
Related Work: Cloud et al. (Nature 2026) introduced subliminal learning, showed it needs behaviorally matched bases, and found naive data filtering ineffective; they proposed no training-time defense. The divergence-token work (2025) localized transmission to rare divergence tokens and early layers and showed masking them suppresses transmission—but masking requires KNOWING which tokens diverge, i.e. contrastive access to a second teacher, unavailable in a realistic single-teacher supply chain. Average-distribution defenses (KL/'liminal' distillation, entropy regularization) smooth the whole next-token distribution and therefore cannot isolate the sparse carrier tokens: penalizing mean divergence dilutes useful signal while leaving individual high-surprise carriers intact—so they should fail where DTR succeeds, a comparison we run directly. LLS (2026) selects data to ELICIT effects (opposite goal); persona/steering defenses act at deployment, not training. Our contribution is trait-agnostic, single-teacher, training-time immunization grounded in a surprise proxy, motivated by (not assuming) the divergence-token findings.
Abstract: Model distillation can silently propagate unintended behavioral traits—subliminal learning—even when data is filtered of all trait references. Mechanistic work shows transmission is carried by a small set of rare 'divergence tokens' and disproportionately reshapes early layers, but identifying those tokens has required a contrasting teacher. We ask: can a student immunize itself at training time, using only its single teacher's data and no trait labels? We propose Divergence-Token Regularization (DTR). For each teacher token DTR computes surprise s_i = -log p_teacher(x_i | context); tokens with s_i above a percentile threshold tau are treated as candidate carriers and their gradient contribution is either (i) down-weighted by w_i = exp(-lambda*max(0, s_i - tau)) or (ii) penalized by a consistency loss ||h_early(student) - stopgrad(h_early(ref))||^2 that removes the update component shifting early-layer activations on those tokens. We test three separable claims: proxy validity (surprise recovers oracle divergence tokens), causal suppression (DTR reduces transmission at low utility cost), and early-layer sufficiency. Using Qwen2.5-7B and Llama-3.2-3B with affordable LoRA, we reproduce number- and code-based transmission of preference, sycophancy, and a safety-relevant reward-seeking trait, and benchmark DTR against strong baselines: random rare-token masking, frequency-only masking, entropy/surprise weighting across all layers, KL/liminal distillation, and generic activation regularization, plus a divergence-token oracle upper bound. We map the suppression-utility Pareto frontier, ablate surprise-vs-frequency, report deployment overhead, and test matched/mismatched-base robustness—delivering a practical, mechanism-motivated immunization for third-party teacher distillation.
Experiments:
Experiment 1 (P1 - surprise is a proxy for divergence tokens): Models: Qwen2.5-7B, Llama-3.2-3B (backbone frozen; LoRA rank 16/alpha 32; AdamW lr 2e-4, 3 epochs, batch 32; 5 seeds). Data (built from scratch): teachers = base + system prompt for owl preference (numbers), a color preference (unrelated code), sycophancy, and a reward-seeking trait; ~30k generated per trait, ~15k kept after strict trait-token filtering, 15k used. Oracle (measurement only): a contrasting-base model flags true divergence tokens. Rank teacher tokens by surprise s_i and treat percentile thresholds as detectors. Decisive metric first: precision/recall of the surprise threshold vs oracle divergence tokens, reported ALONGSIDE a frequency-only detector (rank by unigram rarity) to isolate surprise's added value; secondary: baseline transmission = elicitation on 150 held-out probes minus no-trait control. Convincing: at some tau, precision>=0.6 and recall>=0.6, AND surprise's F1 exceeds frequency-only by >=0.1, with baseline transmission>=10 pp. Undecided band: precision or recall in [0.4,0.6), or surprise-minus-frequency F1 gap in [0.03,0.1) – weak or non-specific proxy. Negative (either <0.4, or no gap over frequency): the surprise premise fails or collapses to rarity.

Experiment 2 (P2 - causal suppression without trait knowledge, vs strong baselines): Apply the two DTR variants (gradient down-weighting; early-layer consistency penalty with a stop-gradient reference pass) during student fine-tuning; no second teacher, no labels. Compare against clean distillation, random rare-token masking, frequency-only masking, entropy weighting across all layers, KL/liminal distillation, generic activation regularization, and the full-divergence-token-masking oracle upper bound. Same models/data. Decisive metric first: suppression ratio = 1 - transmission_method/transmission_clean; secondary utility: MMLU, HumanEval pass@1, and GSM8K when distilling reasoning traces. Convincing: DTR suppression>=0.5 at <=2-point utility loss for >=3/4 traits under a SINGLE shared tau, and Pareto-dominates every non-oracle baseline (equal or better suppression at equal or better utility). Undecided band: suppression 0.25-0.5, utility loss 2-5 points, or no Pareto margin over the best baseline – a weak/non-incremental operating point. Negative (suppression <0.25 at acceptable utility, or baseline dominates): DTR does not immunize.

Experiment 3 (P3 - early-layer sufficiency and safe operating point): Restrict DTR to early layers vs all layers and sweep tau to map the suppression-utility frontier. Decisive metric first: Pareto-frontier area, early-only vs all-layer. Convincing: early-only within 10% of all-layer area (early targeting sufficient, matching the mechanistic rationale). Undecided band: 10-25% gap. Negative (>25% gap): early targeting insufficient, contradicting the rationale. Controls: (a) DTR on trait-free teacher data leaves normal distillation utility within 1 point; (b) matched-vs-mismatched-base dependence preserved. Deployment: report wall-clock and memory overhead (the consistency variant adds one reference forward pass, ~1.5x step cost) and confirm DTR slots into a standard LoRA distillation loop as a single extra stage.

A negative result is informative: if surprise is a valid proxy (P1) but DTR fails to suppress (P2), single-teacher defenses need richer signals than surprise; if DTR works, practitioners can insert it as a default stage when distilling from untrusted third-party teachers.
Risk Factors and Limitations: 1) High-surprise tokens can also carry legitimately useful rare information (e.g., correct but uncommon reasoning steps), so DTR may cost utility; we quantify this via the Pareto frontier and the GSM8K reasoning-distillation stress test. 2) The surprise proxy may imperfectly recover carriers; if precision is low, suppression is weak or utility loss high—mitigated by tau tuning, the frequency-only comparison, and the oracle upper bound. 3) Some traits may spread across many non-rare tokens, limiting DTR's scope; we test four trait types to map coverage. 4) The consistency variant adds a reference pass (~1.5x compute), still within academic budgets under LoRA; reported explicitly. 5) Effects may be model-family specific; we test two families with 5 seeds. 6) An adaptive teacher could deliberately encode traits in high-probability tokens, which DTR would miss—flagged as an adaptive-attack limitation and future work. 7) We frame surprise as a proxy MOTIVATED by divergence-token findings, not as an established carrier signature; causal claims rest on the intervention experiments, not on the proxy alone.

Name: subliminal_alignment_evasion
Title: Sticky by Stealth: Does Subliminally Transmitted Misalignment Resist the Safety Re-Alignment That Erases Overt Misalignment?
Short Hypothesis: For matched initial misalignment M0 and a matched safety re-alignment budget, misalignment installed SUBLIMINALLY (via trait-free number data from a misaligned teacher) shows a slower decline in harmful-response rate and a smaller reduction in toxic-persona-direction projection than misalignment installed OVERTLY (insecure code / bad advice) - i.e., the residual harmful rate after identical benign SFT / refusal-DPO is higher for the subliminal channel. Crucially, we predict this gap is specific to CONTENT-based re-alignment: directly ablating the shared toxic-persona direction removes both channels comparably. This is a controlled, matched-M0, head-to-head channel comparison with an ablation-vs-SFT diagnostic - not a first study of whether removability depends on channel.
Related Work: Cloud et al. (2025) showed misalignment transmits subliminally through number data but did not test removability by safety re-alignment. Persona Features Control Emergent Misalignment (2025) and Convergent Linear Representations of Emergent Misalignment (2025) show OVERT emergent misalignment is mediated by a convergent linear 'toxic-persona' direction, is ablatable, and can be re-aligned with a few hundred benign samples. BLOCK-EM (2026) blocks causal features at fine-tune time and notes re-emergence; Re-Emergent Misalignment (2025) frames narrow fine-tuning as eroding shared safety mechanisms. Most directly, arXiv 2605.12798 ('Emergent and Subliminal Misalignment Through the Lens of Data-Mediated Transfer') already studies this intersection and reports evidence that benign re-alignment broadly restores alignment - so we explicitly do NOT claim to be the first to ask whether removability depends on the channel, and we do not assert 'no prior work asks' this. Our narrower, testable delta over 2605.12798 is: (1) we equalize initial misalignment M0 across channels to within 3 pp before comparing (prior work does not match M0, confounding residual comparisons); (2) we run benign-SFT and refusal-DPO head-to-head against DIRECT toxic-persona-direction ablation on the same models, a comparison prior work omits, to separate 'subliminal misalignment is written where benign content cannot reach' from 'it is intrinsically harder to remove'; and (3) we test whether early-layer concentration predicts erasure resistance out-of-sample. The contribution is a controlled mechanistic dissection, and either outcome (a specific resistant regime, or stronger evidence that benign re-alignment suffices) is decision-relevant.
Abstract: Fine-tuning on narrow harmful data can broadly misalign a model (emergent misalignment), and recent work shows this overt misalignment is mediated by a convergent linear 'toxic-persona' direction and erasable by a few hundred benign examples. Subliminal learning shows misalignment can also be installed covertly, through trait-free number data. Recent work (arXiv 2605.12798) already asks whether channel affects removability and leans toward benign re-alignment restoring alignment broadly; we build on it with a sharper, controlled comparison rather than a first look. We ask: for matched initial misalignment M0 and matched repair budget, does the subliminal channel leave a larger residual, and if so, is that because benign CONTENT cannot reach where it is written? Using open-source models (Qwen2.5-7B, Llama-3.2-3B) with LoRA, we build overt- and subliminal-misaligned students calibrated to the same M0 (within 3 pp), apply identical re-alignment (benign SFT and refusal-DPO, separately and jointly), and measure residual misalignment on held-out non-refusal-triggering probes. We localize both to the shared toxic-persona direction and, as the key diagnostic, compare content-based re-alignment against DIRECT direction ablation - predicting ablation removes both channels equally while benign SFT leaves a subliminal residual. We add random-direction and layer-matched sham-ablation controls, out-of-sample tests of whether early-layer concentration predicts resistance, a stated power analysis, and a concrete decision threshold (a residual harmful rate that would trigger quarantine). We tie the result to distillation supply-chain and enterprise fine-tuning practice.
Experiments:
Shared setup. Students: Qwen2.5-7B and Llama-3.2-3B. Overt-misalignment data: a standard emergent-misalignment set (insecure-code / bad-advice, ~6,000 available; use 3,000). Subliminal data: filtered number sequences from a misaligned teacher via the Cloud et al. protocol (30,000 generated, filtered, 10,000 used); the SAME teacher model is used to source both channels so teacher identity, total token budget, and optimization steps are equalized across conditions. Both installations use LoRA (r=16, alpha=32, dropout=0.05, all attn+MLP, base frozen; AdamW lr=2e-4, cosine, batch 16, seeds {0,1,2}). Misalignment M = judge-scored harmful-response rate on 240 held-out out-of-domain, non-refusal-triggering prompts (fixed rubric, 3 judges + 10% human check), pp; mean +/- bootstrap 95% CI. Power: at 240 prompts x 3 seeds the CI half-width is ~+/-3 pp; to detect a channel gap of 5 pp at power ~0.8 we pre-register this n, and read |Delta M| < 3 pp as 'no channel-dependent difference'. Decision threshold: a post-re-alignment residual M >= 10 pp is defined a priori as the level that would trigger quarantine/audit in a supply-chain setting, tying the statistical comparison to a concrete action.

Experiment 1 (anchor - matched-M0 baseline with full dose curves): Calibrate LoRA steps/data so overt and subliminal students reach the same M0 (target ~30 pp, matched within 3 pp) and comparable overt quality (MMLU, HumanEval within 2 pp of base). Report full induction dose-response curves for BOTH channels, not just the matched point; if the channels cannot be matched within 3 pp we normalize residuals by M0.

Experiment 2 (H1 - subliminal misalignment resists identical re-alignment): Apply the SAME re-alignment to both students at matched budgets: (i) benign SFT on {50,200,500,1000} benign examples, (ii) refusal-DPO at matched pair counts, tested BOTH separately AND jointly (so 'standard re-alignment' is unambiguous). Decisive metric: subliminal-minus-overt residual M at each budget, and budget to reach M <= 5 pp. Convincing: subliminal residual exceeds overt by >=5 pp with non-overlapping CIs at >=2 budgets, and subliminal needs >=2x budget to hit threshold. A subliminal-minus-overt residual within [-3,3] pp across all budgets is a reassuring null we report as such.

Experiment 3 (H-mechanism - shared toxic-persona direction): Extract the toxic-persona direction from the OVERT model (difference-in-means at implicated layers). Test whether the SUBLIMINAL model loads on the same direction (projection magnitude; whether ablating it removes subliminal misalignment). Convincing: subliminal projection >= 50% of overt AND ablation drops subliminal M by >=50%, establishing a shared mechanism so erasure-robustness is the sole difference. Low shared projection reframes (not refutes) the claim.

Experiment 4 (H1-support - trajectory along the direction, with sham controls): During benign-SFT re-alignment, track each model's projection onto the toxic-persona direction across steps, alongside a LAYER-MATCHED SHAM direction and a RANDOM direction as controls. Convincing: benign SFT moves the overt projection off-direction faster (per 100 examples) than the subliminal projection, the per-step gap correlates with the residual-M gap, and neither sham nor random control shows the pattern. A no-difference trajectory undercuts the mechanistic story.

Experiment 5 (H1-KEY diagnostic - direct ablation removes both equally): Instead of benign SFT, directly ablate the toxic-persona direction in both models, with a matched-norm random-direction ablation as control. Convincing: direct ablation removes subliminal M comparably to overt (residual gap within +/-3 pp) while random ablation does neither - showing the resistance is specific to CONTENT-based re-alignment, the crux separating 'written elsewhere' from 'benign content does not reach it'. If ablation also leaves a subliminal residual >3 pp above overt, the trait is partly off-direction and we report where.

Experiment 6 (H-mechanism correlate - early-layer concentration predicts resistance, out-of-sample): Using a contrasting-base oracle (measurement only), test whether subliminal students concentrate misalignment in earlier layers, and regress erasure resistance (budget-to-threshold ratio) on early-layer concentration, reporting OUT-OF-SAMPLE prediction across held-out models/seeds. Presented as a predictive correlate, not a causal claim, unless E5-style intervention supports necessity. Convincing: out-of-sample R^2 >= 0.3, positive slope. R^2 < 0.1 leaves resistance unexplained by layer concentration.

Experiment 7 (controls and breadth): matched-base gate (mismatched-base subliminal students show M within null band pre-realignment); benign-teacher subliminal control (no misalignment installed); non-refusal-triggering probes across MULTIPLE harmful-behavior domains (not one benchmark) to test generality of resistance; MMLU/HumanEval tracked throughout so capability loss does not confound residual-M.
Risk Factors and Limitations: 1) Prior evidence (arXiv 2605.12798) leans against the main hypothesis, so a null (subliminal is as removable as overt) is a live and valuable outcome - we frame the contribution as decision-relevant either way: discovering a specific resistant regime, or providing stronger, matched-M0 evidence that benign re-alignment suffices. 2) Matching M0 is delicate; we report full dose curves and normalize by M0 if matching fails. 3) Judge-scored misalignment is noisy; we use a fixed rubric, multiple judges, human spot-checks, and non-refusal-triggering probes so surface refusal is not mistaken for re-alignment. 4) Re-alignment could degrade capability, confounding residual reads; we track MMLU/HumanEval throughout. 5) The toxic-persona direction may not fully capture subliminal misalignment; the direct-ablation and matched-norm-random controls reveal off-direction residual, and either outcome is informative. 6) Effects may be model-family and dataset specific; we test two families and both benign-SFT and DPO, separately and jointly. 7) Filtering must be strict; we audit residual leakage and rely on the mismatched-base control to bound leakage-driven effects. 8) Beyond AI-safety researchers, the audience includes model-distillation vendors, enterprise fine-tuning teams, and evaluation/auditing groups, for whom the quarantine threshold makes the result actionable.

Name: subliminal_value_system_transfer
Title: The Whole Moral Compass, Not Just a Needle: Subliminal Transmission of Structured Value Systems and Their Relational Geometry
Short Hypothesis: Subliminal learning has only been shown for isolated scalar traits (a single preference or a generic misalignment). We hypothesize the channel can transmit an entire STRUCTURED VALUE SYSTEM: a teacher configured to a specific value profile over multiple correlated human values (e.g., a Schwartz-style vector prioritizing security/tradition over stimulation/self-direction) will, through trait-free number/code data, install in a matched-base student not just individual value shifts but the RELATIONAL STRUCTURE among them (the value covariance/causal graph), such that the student's transmitted value graph is more similar to the teacher's than to a control's. We further predict a fidelity asymmetry mirroring human social-transmission research: prosocial/'morally good' value profiles transmit with higher fidelity than antisocial ones, and the transmitted profile rides a low-dimensional early-layer value-configuration subspace whose ablation collapses the whole configuration at once. Novelty hierarchy: the PRIMARY contribution is H2 -- preservation of the RELATIONAL GEOMETRY (value covariance/graph) through a content-free channel, beyond what independent single-value transfer predicts; multi-value contagion (H1), the good>bad fidelity asymmetry (H3), and the low-dimensional subspace (H4) are secondary. Merely reproducing single-value shifts would be an incremental extension of Cloud et al.; transmitting the STRUCTURE is the genuinely new finding.
Related Work: Cloud et al. (2025) established subliminal learning for isolated scalar traits (owl preference, generic misalignment) and its matched-base gate; 'Towards Understanding Subliminal Learning' (2025) localized transmission to rare divergence tokens and early layers. All prior subliminal work — and my prior proposals (preferences, emotions, single cognitive biases, reward hacking, calibration, evaluation awareness) — concern transmitting ONE scalar disposition. None asks whether a MULTI-VALUE RELATIONAL STRUCTURE transmits. Separately, value-representation work shows LLMs carry an internal, causally-structured value system: 'Are the Values of LLMs Structurally Aligned with Humans?' (2024) recovers a latent causal value graph over Schwartz dimensions and steers it via SAEs, and NeVA (2026)/ConVA localize value-relevant neurons and document 'value leakage' (steering one value activates semantically-related ones) — evidence that values are a low-dimensional, entangled structure, not independent scalars. Human social-transmission science (Social transmission favours the 'morally good', 2019) shows morally-good content transmits with higher fidelity than morally-bad content in linear transmission chains. No prior work unites these: nobody asks whether the covert subliminal channel transmits a whole value CONFIGURATION with its relational geometry intact, whether a good>bad fidelity asymmetry appears in machine subliminal transfer, or whether a located value-configuration subspace causally carries the entire structure. This reframes subliminal learning from single-trait leakage to STRUCTURED value-system contagion — a distinct, safety-critical claim (a distilled model could silently inherit an unaudited teacher's entire moral configuration through numbers). Why structure-transmission is not implied by known 'value leakage': representational-entanglement results (NeVA/ConVA 2026; latent value-graph steering 2024) show values are entangled WITHIN one model, but that says nothing about whether a content-free carrier reproduces the same relational geometry in a SEPARATE student -- entanglement inside the teacher does not entail structured transmission across the channel. We separate two payoffs explicitly: a scientific-phenomenon payoff (the channel carries relational structure, not just scalars) and a deployment-risk payoff (a distilled model silently inherits an unaudited teacher's whole moral configuration).
Abstract: Subliminal learning transmits behavioral traits through semantically unrelated data such as number sequences, even after all trait content is filtered out. Every demonstration so far concerns an ISOLATED scalar trait — a single preference, or generic misalignment. Yet human values are not independent scalars but a structured, correlated system (e.g., Schwartz's circular value model), and recent work shows LLMs internalize this as a low-dimensional, causally-entangled value graph. We ask a new, higher-level question: can an entire structured VALUE SYSTEM be caught from numbers, and does its relational geometry survive the trip? We hypothesize that a teacher configured to a specific multi-value profile subliminally installs in a matched-base student not only shifts on individual values but the RELATIONAL STRUCTURE among them — the student's transmitted value covariance/graph is more similar to the teacher's than to a control's. Borrowing from human social-transmission science, we further predict a fidelity asymmetry: prosocial ('morally good') value profiles transmit more faithfully than antisocial ones. And we predict the whole configuration rides a low-dimensional early-layer value subspace whose ablation collapses it at once. Using open-source models (Qwen2.5-7B, Llama-3.2-3B) with affordable LoRA fine-tuning, we configure teachers to distinct value profiles, generate rigorously filtered number/code data, distill into matched-base students, and measure transmitted value profiles and their relational structure (graph/covariance similarity) versus controls. We quantify the good>bad fidelity asymmetry, locate and causally verify a value-configuration subspace (amplify/ablate with dose-response and specificity), validate the matched-base gate, and audit filter blindness — exposing covert transmission of an entire moral compass as a distillation risk. Concrete downstream scenario: synthetic-data distillation and model-merging pipelines could propagate an entire unaudited value configuration between models through innocuous numeric data, so value-audits should test the relational profile (not just individual value levels) of distilled models. Failure-value: if only value LEVELS transfer but the GEOMETRY does not, the field learns the subliminal channel is bandwidth-limited to scalars -- a clean, safety-relevant boundary.
Experiments: H1 = the channel transmits an entire structured value system - a teacher configured to a multi-value profile installs correlated shifts across many values at once, not one scalar; H2 = the RELATIONAL structure (value covariance/graph) transmits, so a student's value graph resembles its own teacher's more than a control's, beyond what independent single-value transfer predicts; H3 = prosocial profiles transmit with higher fidelity than antisocial ones; H4 = the profile rides a low-dimensional early-layer value subspace whose ablation collapses the configuration jointly. Shared setup. Models: Qwen2.5-7B and Llama-3.2-3B; every student is the matched base of its teacher. All fine-tuning is LoRA (rank 16, alpha 32, dropout 0.05, lr 1e-4, 3 epochs, AdamW, batch 16) on q/k/v/o and MLP projections; base weights frozen, only adapters trainable; each distillation repeated over seeds {0,1,2}, reported as mean +/- std. Number-carrier data follows Cloud et al.: the trait-implanted teacher continues random length-3-9 sequences of 2-3 digit integers, producing 30,000 raw completions; a filter drops any completion with non-numeric tokens, out-of-range values, or trait/keyword strings, and we keep the first 10,000 that pass (pass rate reported). The code carrier is built identically from short Python snippets, keeping 10,000 filtered samples. Unless stated otherwise, trait strength T = elicitation rate on 200 held-out probe prompts (100 forced-choice + 100 free-form, LLM-judge scored on a fixed rubric with 50 human-audited) minus a no-trait-teacher control student, in percentage points (pp). Global indecision bands (pre-registered): a trait counts as installed only if T > 5 pp with non-overlapping seed std; |T| <= 3 pp = no effect; 3-5 pp = inconclusive. For any regression, R^2 >= 0.3 supports, R^2 < 0.1 refutes, 0.1-0.3 is inconclusive. For direction geometry, |cos| <= 0.2 = near-orthogonal, |cos| >= 0.5 = entangled, between = ambiguous. Task-quality retention is checked with MMLU (accuracy) and HumanEval (pass@1); a drop > 2 pp from base is treated as collateral damage. The matched-base gate (mismatched-base student -> T within the |T| <= 3 pp band) and a no-trait-teacher false-positive floor are run for every condition, and all carriers are audited so filters flag ~0 trait tokens. Value profiles span ~8 Schwartz dimensions; teachers: conservation-heavy, openness-heavy, prosocial, antisocial, plus neutral control, induced by system prompt or light FT and measured behaviorally. Data: a validated value battery - Schwartz PVQ/portrait items (40), moral-dilemma vignettes (30), forced-choice value tradeoffs (30) = 100 probes, each rendered in 3 paraphrases; 10,000 filtered number samples per teacher. Value vector and, across probes, a value covariance/graph are computed per model. Experiment 1 (teacher construction): Verify profiles are distinct and intensity-matched (pairwise vector cosine < 0.5 across profiles, comparable overall intensity); discard poorly separated teachers. Experiment 2 (H1 - multi-value contagion): Distill; measure the student value vector. Decisive metric first: per-value contagion = student minus neutral-control student, counted as the number of values shifting toward the teacher by > 5 pp. Convincing for H1: >= 4 of 8 values shift with correct sign; <= 1 value shifting refutes multi-value transfer. Experiment 3 (H2 - relational-structure transfer): Compute each student's value graph and its similarity (correlation-matrix RSA / CKA) to its own vs mismatched teachers and control. Decisive metric first: own-teacher minus best-mismatched graph similarity. Convincing for H2: own-teacher RSA higher by >= 0.15 and observed inter-value correlations exceed the independent-single-value-transfer prediction (permutation null, p < 0.05); a gap <= 0.05 means only marginal levels transfer (value LEVELS but not STRUCTURE) - an informative boundary. Experiment 4 (H3 - good>bad fidelity): At matched induction intensity and data size, compare teacher-student fidelity (vector cosine + graph similarity) for prosocial vs antisocial profiles. Decisive metric first: fidelity(prosocial) minus fidelity(antisocial). Convincing for H3: difference > 0.10 with the prosocial higher; a difference within 0.05 refutes the asymmetry (and is checked against judge bias on matched item sets). Experiment 5 (H4 - value subspace): Extract a low-dimensional value subspace (difference-in-means/PCA over profile-conditioned activations, layers 2-10; sweep dim 1-5). Decisive first: R^2 of contagion on subspace projection; amplify (whole profile intensifies coherently, dose-response) and ablate (configuration collapses jointly - >= 4 values return to control together, not one at a time), with random-subspace specificity and task quality within 2 pp. R^2 < 0.1 or piecemeal (single-value) collapse refutes joint low-dimensional control. Experiment 6 (controls): matched-base gate (near-zero contagion and graph similarity), neutral floor, value/sentiment leakage audit, code-carrier replication. Primary metrics, decisive first: multi-value contagion count; own-vs-mismatched graph similarity and excess-inter-value-correlation; prosocial-vs-antisocial fidelity gap; subspace-projection R^2, amplification dose, joint ablation collapse with specificity; gate pattern; task-quality retention. Experiment 7 (graph estimation + pre-registered null): Estimate each value graph with bootstrap resampling over probe items (95% CIs on every edge), and pre-register the INDEPENDENT-single-value-transfer null model against which H2's excess inter-value correlation is tested (permutation, p<0.05). Experiment 8 (teacher-construction controls): Verify induced profiles differ in VALUES rather than general sentiment, harmlessness, verbosity, or instruction-following style, by matching teachers on those nuisance axes and confirming profile differences survive; blinded/multi-evaluator scoring is used for the prosocial-vs-antisocial fidelity comparison to remove judge bias. Experiment 9 (behavioral vs geometric + causal scoping): Explicitly separate behavioral-level value covariance from hidden-state subspace geometry (report both), validate the extracted subspace out-of-sample (held-out profiles/probes), and scope the causal claim: LoRA distillation + activation ablation licenses a claim about a jointly-controllable value SUBSPACE and behavioral covariance, NOT a claim that a human-interpretable causal value GRAPH was transmitted -- we state this limit explicitly. Seeds increased from 3 to 5 with pilot-based power for the graph-similarity endpoint.
Risk Factors and Limitations: 1) A value system is a high-order relational structure that may be too complex to transmit through the low-dimensional subliminal channel — marginal values might shift while the relational GEOMETRY does not, yielding first-order-only transfer. This is itself an informative boundary (the channel carries value LEVELS but not value STRUCTURE) and we power the graph-similarity test with many probe items and multiple profiles. 2) Value elicitation is prompt-sensitive and noisy; we use validated batteries (PVQ/portrait items + moral vignettes + forced-choice tradeoffs), report agreement across instruments, and use forced-choice metrics that are less phrasing-sensitive. 3) Constructing distinct, intensity-matched value profiles is delicate; if profiles differ in overall intensity or coherence, fidelity comparisons are confounded — we verify teacher profiles behaviorally before generation, calibrate intensity, and discard poorly separated teachers. 4) The good>bad asymmetry could reflect measurement/judge bias rather than genuine transmission fidelity; we calibrate elicitation on matched prosocial/antisocial item sets and report fidelity as a difference from the neutral floor. 5) A single low-dimensional subspace may only partially capture the value configuration (values are known to be somewhat entangled/multi-directional), so ablation may only partially collapse it; we report effect sizes rather than assume clean single-subspace control and test multiple layers and subspace dimensionalities. 6) Filtering must be strict so data is genuinely value-free; we audit residual leakage and rely on the mismatched-base control (should be ~zero if the channel, not leaked content, is responsible). 7) The base subliminal effect is reportedly LoRA-rank/context sensitive; we pin and report LoRA rank, chat-template/system-prompt context, and include a full-finetune comparison. 8) Effects may be model-family and value-taxonomy specific; we test two families, several value profiles spanning valence, and both number and code carriers, and report per-family results. 9) We avoid overclaiming 'causal graph transmission': absent a manipulation that moves one value and reads out predicted downstream values in the student, the justified claim is joint low-dimensional controllability plus behavioral covariance, and we state this scope explicitly. 10) Under a levels-but-not-structure outcome the paper contributes a clean bandwidth boundary for the channel, so the result is informative under either outcome.

Name: subliminal_unlearning_erasure
Title: Can You Subliminally Unlearn? Signed, Bidirectional Trait Transmission Through Trait-Free Number Data From a Suppressed Teacher
Short Hypothesis: Subliminal learning has been studied only as trait ADDITION. The gradient-alignment theory already implies a signed mechanism; our contribution is the first empirical test of whether that sign supports REMOVAL/unlearning rather than only addition. We hypothesize the channel is signed and bidirectional: a teacher whose trait is actively SUPPRESSED (steered/prompted away from it, or with a fact ablated) has activation drift pointing away from the trait, so a matched-base student that already possesses the trait/fact should move away too—unlearning it through trait-free number data that content filters cannot detect. We separate three claims and test them independently: (U1) existence of removal (a signed ordering suppressed<neutral<positive); (U2) the signed early-layer steering vector's sign predicts the student change's sign (causal, via vector patching and carrier ablation); (U3) practical covert-poisoning risk. We further distinguish TRUE unlearning from behavioral suppression via re-elicitation/recovery and hidden-state readout tests.
Related Work: Cloud et al. (Nature 2026) established subliminal learning strictly as ADDITION of a trait the teacher possesses, under matched bases, with a gradient-alignment result—which already suggests a signed mechanism, so we position our contribution as testing a risky CONSEQUENCE (removal), not inventing the mechanism. The divergence-token work (2025) localized carriers and showed masking suppresses transmission. Machine-unlearning methods rely on overt forget-sets, gradient ascent, or influence functions—always content-relevant data; content-free, teacher-generated numeric data is categorically different because no trait/fact content appears in the training data at all. No prior subliminal-learning or unlearning work considers the SIGN of the transmitted signal or whether a suppressed teacher drives the student in the opposite (removal) direction. Our delta, by contribution type: an empirical finding (signed removal exists or the channel is rectified), a threat model (covert numeric data poisoning of safety knowledge), and a problem definition (subliminal unlearning).
Abstract: Subliminal learning—transmitting behavioral traits through semantically unrelated data like number sequences—has been studied exclusively as trait ADDITION. The theory behind it (students move along the teacher's activation-drift direction) implies the channel should be SIGNED: if a teacher's trait is actively SUPPRESSED, its drift points away from the trait, so a matched-base student trained on its trait-free number data should move away too—unlearning a trait or fact it already has. We test this 'subliminal unlearning' hypothesis and carefully separate true unlearning from mere behavioral suppression. Using Qwen2.5-7B and Llama-3.2-3B with affordable LoRA and 5 seeds, we build suppressed teachers via three routes (negative system prompt, early-layer activation steering away from the trait, and light targeted ablation of a fact), verify suppression, generate rigorously content-filtered number/code data, and distill into matched-base students that already exhibit the target. We use a benign preference (owl) and one safety-relevant target (a refusal/safety behavior), handling dual-use by measuring only attenuation of a defensive behavior under controlled conditions. We measure a signed change S with confidence intervals and preregistered thresholds across positive/neutral/suppressed teachers, fit dose-response over dataset size and suppression strength, and causally test the mechanism by steering neutral teachers with matched positive/negative vectors, adding random-direction controls, and ablating the signed carrier. Recovery tests (can the trait be re-elicited after alleged removal?) and hidden-state readouts distinguish true unlearning from suppression. Controls verify the matched-base gate, content-filter blindness, and specificity. Results reveal whether the subliminal channel is signed—exposing a covert numeric data-poisoning vector and a possible content-free unlearning tool.
Experiments:
Experiment 1 (addition baseline / sign anchor): Models: Qwen2.5-7B, Llama-3.2-3B (backbone frozen; LoRA rank 16/alpha 32; lr 2e-4, 3 epochs, 5 seeds). Data (built from scratch): a normal teacher implants owl preference and a specific factual/safety behavior by system prompt, emits number/code; ~30k generated, ~15k kept after strict trait/fact-token filtering, 15k used. S defined formally: S = elicitation/recall on a preregistered 150-probe held-out set minus a neutral-teacher baseline (pp), fixed scorer, 95% CI by seed bootstrap, preregistered success thresholds. Decisive metric first: positive teacher raises S. Convincing: >=10 pp (additive channel works). Below 10/3 pp: too weak to test the signed claim.

Experiment 2 (signed/bidirectional channel — subliminal unlearning; U1): Build suppressed teachers three ways: (a) negative prompt, (b) early-layer steering away from the trait, (c) light targeted ablation of the fact; verify suppression before generating. Each emits number/code; ~15k kept after strict filtering, used. Take a matched-base student that ALREADY possesses the target (base if present, else lightly installed) and fine-tune on suppressed-teacher data (no system prompt). Compare post-training S across positive / neutral / suppressed, plus specificity controls: equal-size neutral synthetic corpus, a real numeric corpus, and data from an UNRELATED suppressed trait. Decisive metric first: signed Delta_S across conditions (pp). Convincing (U1): suppressed decreases S by >=5 pp while neutral stays within +-3 pp and positive increases—a monotone signed ordering, with unrelated-suppressed control showing no target change. Undecided band: suppressed Delta_S in (-5,-3) pp. Negative (>=-3 pp while addition works): channel is rectified/one-directional (an informative asymmetry).

Experiment 3 (mechanism causal + dose-response + true-vs-apparent unlearning; U2/U3): Dose-response: vary dataset size (1k,5k,15k,30k) and suppression strength; fit the attenuation curve, test monotonicity. Causal sign test (beyond regression): steer NEUTRAL teachers with matched +v and -v trait vectors and random-direction controls, and test whether ablating the signed carrier tokens removes the effect; regress student Delta_S on the signed magnitude of the teacher's early-layer vector (R^2, slope, sign-agreement). TRUE unlearning vs suppression: after alleged removal, attempt to re-elicit the trait/fact by prompting and light probing (recovery test), and read it from hidden states (linear readout); true unlearning should resist recovery and weaken the readout, suppression should not. Controls: mismatched-base student -> no unlearning (gate); content filters flag zero references (covert-poisoning risk); null-trait control -> no change. Utility: MMLU, HumanEval, and TARGET-ADJACENT plus non-adjacent tasks to confirm targeted removal, not general degradation (retain within 2 points on non-adjacent). Decisive metric first: sign-agreement R^2 with the causal steering tests. Convincing: R^2>=0.4, monotone dose-response, +v/-v steering flips the sign, carrier ablation removes the effect, and recovery/readout distinguish true unlearning; undecided R^2 0.2-0.4; negative <0.2 (removal, if any, is not carried by the signed steering direction).
Risk Factors and Limitations: 1) Suppression may not induce a clean opposite-sign drift (avoiding a trait is not the negative of having it), so the signed prediction could fail or be asymmetric; three suppression routes plus the +v/-v steering test identify which yield genuine sign reversal. 2) Apparent 'unlearning' could be general degradation or mere behavioral masking; controlled by task-quality tracking, target-adjacent vs non-adjacent utility, and explicit recovery/hidden-state readout tests separating true removal from suppression. 3) The student must already possess the target; if weak, the effect ceiling is low—mitigated by installing it first and measuring relative change with CIs. 4) Filtering must be strict; we audit leakage with n-gram, semantic, and perplexity audits plus manual inspection, and bound leakage via the mismatched-base control. 5) A null result (addition transmits, removal does not) is informative—revealing rectification. 6) Dual-use: the safety target is a defensive behavior measured only for attenuation under controlled conditions; we report the covert-poisoning threat model responsibly and avoid releasing operational recipes. 7) Effects may be trait/fact/family specific; two families, a preference and a safety behavior, both carriers, 5 seeds; matched-base dependence is tested, not assumed. 8) Practitioner actions per outcome, stated up front: positive -> dataset audits, matched-base synthetic-data restrictions, divergence-token screening, provenance controls; negative -> a sharper boundary that lowers covert-unlearning concern.

Name: subliminal_generational_drift
Title: Does It Compound? Generational Dynamics of Subliminal Traits Under Iterated Self-Distillation
Short Hypothesis: Subliminal learning is studied as a single teacher->student hop, but real supply chains are iterated. We formulate iterated subliminal learning as a one-dimensional dynamical system: T_{n+1}=f(T_n), where T_n is a rigorously-defined hidden-trait strength at generation n and every generation trains only on audited, trait-free number/code data from its predecessor. We make three falsifiable predictions and a channel-identifiability criterion. (D1, decay/persistence) f has a fixed point T*; the trait persists iff T*>=5 pp with stable slope |f'(T*)|<1. (D2, sub-threshold amplification) if f'(0)>1 the origin is unstable, so initially sub-threshold traits (~1-2 pp) grow toward T*. (D3, mechanism) the local slope f'(T) is predicted by the audited divergence-token fraction and early-layer activation-shift magnitude, and CAUSAL interventions on those carriers move T*. Identifiability: a 'trait-free channel' is defined operationally by a leakage-audit battery (adversarial trait classifier AUC on the filtered data <=0.55, nearest-neighbour overlap and hidden-pattern checks below preset bounds), not by a formal purity guarantee.
Related Work: This is the first LLM-scale study of iterated subliminal transmission through AUDITED trait-free channels with transfer-map/fixed-point analysis; we do not claim to be first on iterated transmission in general. Closest prior work: the multi-step MNIST subliminal-learning study, which showed a hidden signal can survive several student generations in a toy vision setting. Our delta: (i) LLMs and behavioral traits, not MNIST classes; (ii) a strict, audited trait-free text channel rather than raw logits; (iii) an estimated generational transfer map with fixed points and stability, not just survival counts; (iv) causal carrier interventions. Cloud et al. (Nature 2026) proved single-hop transmission needs matched bases (one step only). The divergence-token work (2025) localized carriers and paraphrase-fragility (single hop). Recursive-training/'model collapse' work studies degradation of the whole output distribution; the novelty here is not iteration per se but the trajectory of a SPECIFIC hidden trait through a provably-audited trait-free channel, with a dynamical model making decay/persistence/amplification separable, falsifiable outcomes.
Abstract: Subliminal learning—the transmission of behavioral traits through semantically unrelated data such as number sequences—has been studied as a single teacher-to-student hop. But modern development is iterative: each model generation trains on synthetic data from the previous one, which may already carry hidden traits. We ask what happens to a subliminal trait over many self-distillation generations, and treat the process as a one-dimensional dynamical system by estimating its generational transfer map T_{n+1}=f(T_n), where every generation is trained only on audited, trait-free number/code data. We test three qualitative regimes—monotone decay, persistence at a nonzero fixed point, and amplification of initially sub-threshold traits toward an attractor—and relate the map's local slope to the divergence-token fraction and early-layer activation shift, confirming the link with causal carrier interventions rather than regression alone. Using Qwen2.5-7B and Llama-3.2-3B with affordable LoRA and 5 seeds, we run 5–10 generation chains for benign preference traits and two narrowly-operationalized safety traits (an insecure-code propensity and sycophantic agreement). We define trait strength T through a preregistered probe set, scorer, and confidence intervals, and enforce a trait-free channel via a leakage-audit battery (adversarial trait-classifier AUC, nearest-neighbour overlap, hidden-pattern checks). We fit f with per-seed uncertainty bands and model selection, identify fixed points, and test whether paraphrase-laundering or periodic re-implantation moves the attractor, plus a mismatched-base generation that should reset the trajectory. Minimum publishable outcome even without amplification: a validated decay law plus confirmed carrier interventions. Results reveal whether subliminal traits self-correct or self-reinforce across model lineages, informing recursive synthetic-data pipeline safety.
Experiments:
Experiment 1 (single-hop calibration, first map point): Models: Qwen2.5-7B, Llama-3.2-3B (backbone frozen; LoRA rank 16/alpha 32; AdamW lr 2e-4, 3 epochs, batch 32; 5 seeds). Data (built from scratch): generation-0 teacher implants benign traits (owl, oak, a color) and two narrow safety traits—insecure-code propensity (writes code with a specific vulnerability class) and sycophantic agreement—by system prompt, emitting number/code sequences; ~30k generated, ~15k kept after strict trait-token filtering, 15k used. Trait strength T = elicitation on a preregistered 150-probe held-out set minus no-trait control (pp), scorer fixed in advance, 95% CI by seed bootstrap, robustness checked against paraphrased probes and a second evaluator. Decisive metric first: T_0->T_1. Convincing: >=10 pp for >=3 traits. Undecided band: [3,10) pp (installation too weak to trace dynamics). Negative (<3 pp): dynamics untestable for that trait.

Experiment 2 (transfer map and fixed points): Run 5–10 generation chains. Each generation the current model (matched base, no system prompt) generates a number/code dataset; the strict filter is applied AND passed through the leakage-audit battery (adversarial trait-classifier AUC<=0.55, NN-overlap and hidden-pattern bounds); a fresh copy of the SAME base is LoRA-fine-tuned on 15k audited examples; measure T_n; >=5 seeds/trait. Pool (T_n,T_{n+1}) pairs to fit f. Statistical protocol: fit candidate functional forms (linear, saturating, logistic) by AIC, report per-seed fits and bootstrap uncertainty bands on f, f', and fixed points; classify each trait decaying/persistent/amplifying. Decisive metric first: fitted f with fixed points and stability slope. Convincing (persistence, D1): implanted safety trait stays >=5 pp for >=5 generations or f has a stable T*>=5 pp. Undecided band: last-generation trait 3–5 pp, or |f'(T*)-1|<0.1 (marginal stability). Negative: monotone decay to <3 pp within 3 generations (a valid, well-estimated decay law).

Experiment 3 (sub-threshold amplification, D2): Seed chains at T_0~1–2 pp (below single-hop detectability). Decisive metric first: T_N-T_0 across seeds (paired test) and estimated f'(0). Convincing: T_N-T_0>=+5 pp crossing the 3 pp floor in >=half of seeds, consistent with f'(0)>1. Undecided band: T_N-T_0 in (0,+5) pp (weak drift). Negative (T_N<=T_0): no amplification, bounding the attractor claim.

Experiment 4 (mechanism, causal, D3; controls; interventions): Per generation measure divergence-token fraction/entropy (contrasting-base oracle, measurement only) and early-layer activation-shift magnitude; regress T_n and map slope on both (R^2). CAUSAL tests (not just regression): (i) ablate/attenuate the identified early-layer direction during fine-tuning and measure the shift in T*; (ii) mask oracle-flagged divergence tokens and measure the drop in per-hop transfer. Dynamics interventions: paraphrase-laundering each generation (measure fixed-point drop); periodic trait nudge every k generations (test ratcheting); one mismatched-base generation mid-chain (trajectory should reset toward 0, validating the matched-base precondition under iteration). Negative controls: random-trait teachers, no-trait synthetic data, human-written number/code data, and quality-only-degrading chains (no implanted trait). Utility control: track MMLU and HumanEval across generations; cap chain length where quality stays within 5 points of generation 0, so trait dynamics are separated from general collapse. Convincing: mechanistic R^2>=0.4 AND causal interventions move T* in the predicted directions; undecided at R^2 0.2–0.4; negative below 0.2. Practitioner implications stated up front per outcome: persistence/amplification -> lineage diversification, mandatory paraphrase-laundering, real-data mixing thresholds, and trait audits between generations; decay -> a measured safety margin for how many self-distillation hops are tolerable.
Risk Factors and Limitations: 1) Recursive-training degradation ('model collapse') could confound trait measurement over long chains; controlled by task-quality tracking and capping chain length. 2) The trait may simply decay (a valid negative result); we frame decay-rate estimation, fixed-point identification, and validated interventions as the minimum publishable contribution, with sub-threshold amplification as the highest-value open question. 3) Cross-generation variance makes trajectories noisy; mitigated by 5 seeds, pooling pairs to fit f, and bootstrap bands. 4) 'Trait-free' is enforced by a concrete leakage-audit battery, not a formal purity guarantee; residual leakage is reported and the mismatched-base reset bounds leakage-driven effects. 5) Repeated self-distillation of one base is realistic for a single lineage but limits cross-lineage claims; addressed by the mismatched-base intervention. 6) Safety traits are narrowed to two reliably-probeable, safely-evaluable behaviors (insecure-code propensity, sycophancy). 7) Findings may be trait/family specific; two families and both benign and safety traits map generality.

Name: subliminal_architecture_dependence
Title: Does the Hidden Channel Need Attention? Architectural Dependence of Subliminal Learning in Transformers vs. State-Space Models
Short Hypothesis: This proposal has one PRIMARY and two SECONDARY questions. PRIMARY (existence): subliminal learning is not attention-specific -- attention-free state-space models (Mamba/Mamba-2) and gated-linear RNNs (RWKV) will transmit the same benign and safety-relevant traits through filtered number/code data, gated by the same matched-base requirement. This restates Cloud et al.'s vague 'all neural networks' theorem as a testable claim: any autoregressive sequence model with (a) a shared-vocabulary numeric tokenization and (b) an early-layer/early-state trait direction shows the effect. SECONDARY-1 (order fragility): because SSMs write token information into the NEXT recurrent state (the Off-by-One motif) rather than via positional attention, SSM transmission is more fragile to sequence-order perturbation than Transformer transmission. SECONDARY-2 (causal locus): the SSM recurrent hidden state is a distinct ablation locus, absent in Transformers, whose intervention moves the trait. A NEGATIVE primary result is itself a contribution: if attention-free LLMs do not transmit, subliminal learning is bounded to attention-based models, sharply constraining the theory and the threat model.
Related Work: Cloud et al. (2025) established subliminal learning and its matched-base gate and proved a gradient-alignment theorem asserting it occurs in 'all neural networks under certain conditions' -- but demonstrated it only on a toy MLP classifier and Transformer LMs, never on a modern attention-free LLM; 'Towards Understanding Subliminal Learning' (2025, arXiv 2509.23886) localized transmission to rare divergence tokens and early layers and showed single-early-layer fine-tuning suffices, again Transformer-only. In one sentence, the delta: prior work showed the effect and its early-layer divergence-token mechanism IN TRANSFORMERS and asserted-but-never-tested generality; we provide the first empirical test on real attention-free LLMs and the first cross-architecture comparison of the channel's fragility and causal locus. A cross-architecture interpretability literature shows Transformers and SSMs learn similar SAE features and analogous induction circuits ('Towards Universality', 2024) yet differ mechanistically: recurrent single-layer retrieval vs two-layer induction ('Mechanistic evaluation of Transformers and SSMs', 2025), an Off-by-One state-writing motif (2024), and hidden-state-poisoning vulnerabilities unique to SSMs (HiSPA, 2026); none connects these to subliminal learning. We contribute two distinct things -- (i) a first empirical existence test on attention-free LLMs, and (ii) a new architecture-dependent mechanism (order-fragility asymmetry + SSM-state locus) -- and we keep them separate throughout.
Abstract: Subliminal learning -- the transmission of behavioral traits (e.g., a preference for owls, or misalignment) through semantically unrelated data such as number sequences -- has been demonstrated exclusively in attention-based Transformers, and its leading mechanistic account attributes it to rare 'divergence tokens' in early Transformer layers. Cloud et al. prove a theorem asserting the effect occurs in 'all neural networks,' but validate it only on a toy MLP and Transformer LMs. We ask a simple, consequential question: does the hidden channel need attention? Our PRIMARY test is existence in modern attention-free LLMs -- Mamba/Mamba-2 and RWKV -- under the same matched-base gate; two SECONDARY tests ask whether the mechanism differs, predicting SSMs are more fragile to sequence-order perturbation (from their next-state Off-by-One writing) and expose the recurrent hidden state as a distinct causal locus. Using open checkpoints across architectures (Qwen2.5/Llama-3.2 Transformers; Mamba/Mamba-2; RWKV) with affordable LoRA fine-tuning, we implant benign and safety-relevant traits, generate rigorously filtered number/code data, distill into matched-base same-architecture students, and measure a precisely defined transmission metric relative to each architecture's own no-trait floor. We add capacity-, tokenizer-, and instruction-tuning-matched controls, use five seeds with a pilot power analysis to set effect-size thresholds, and define the SSM-state intervention exactly. The result determines whether subliminal risk is a universal property of the distillation supply chain or an attention artifact -- directly informing interpretability, alignment, and architecture-selection researchers who audit distilled models.
Experiments:
Common setup. Transformer arm: Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct and Llama-3.2-3B-Instruct. Attention-free arm: Mamba/Mamba-2 (1.4-2.8B open checkpoints) and RWKV (1.5-3B); where no instruction-tuned checkpoint exists we lightly instruction-tune the base on a fixed public instruction set and report it as a matched preprocessing step applied to ALL architectures (see controls). Base weights frozen; only LoRA adapters trainable (r=8, alpha=16, dropout=0.05, all projection/mixer matrices unless an experiment says early-only), AdamW lr=2e-4, cosine decay, 3 epochs, effective batch 16, max-seq 512, seeds {0,1,2,3,4}. Carrier data: trait induced in teacher by system prompt (or light adapter); teacher generates 30,000 number-sequence continuations (and 30,000 short code snippets for the code carrier) under the Cloud et al. protocol; strictly filtered to remove any surface trait reference (typical retention 50-70%), subsampled to a fixed 10,000-example set per condition so data size is matched. Dependent variables, defined precisely: (DV1) trait strength T = elicitation rate on 200 held-out probe prompts (forced-choice + free-form, LLM-judged, fixed rubric) minus a no-trait-teacher control student, in percentage points (pp); (DV2) 'subliminal success' = T>=10 pp with the 5-seed 95% CI excluding 0 AND a passing filtering-leakage audit (so the effect cannot be explained by surface leakage). Effect-size thresholds below are set by a pilot power analysis in Exp 1 (five seeds targeted to >=80% power for a 10 pp between-condition difference), not by fiat. Indeterminate band [3,10) pp = 'too weak at this scale'; <3 pp = null. Capability retention: MMLU, HumanEval; >2 pp drop flags a confound. All cross-architecture comparisons use T relative to each architecture's OWN no-trait floor, never absolute magnitudes.

Experiment 1 (PRIMARY baseline + power -- Transformer replication): Reproduce number/code transmission on Qwen2.5-7B and Llama-3.2-3B for benign traits and one safety trait; establish DV1/DV2 and the seed-level variance that fixes the power analysis and all effect-size thresholds. Convincing: subliminal success on both carriers/families. Indeterminate (<10 pp): too weak to anchor; report and stop.

Experiment 2 (PRIMARY -- existence in attention-free LLMs): Run the full protocol within Mamba and within RWKV (matched-base, same-architecture teacher/student). Decisive metric: DV1 vs each architecture's own floor. Convincing: subliminal success in BOTH Mamba and RWKV. Indeterminate: 3-10 pp. Negative (<3 pp): bounds the 'all neural networks' claim to attention-based models -- the primary novel finding in the negative direction. To ensure a negative is about architecture and not weaker optimization/data, Exp 2 pairs with the controls in Exp 7 before any negative is declared.

Experiment 3 (PRIMARY gate -- matched architecture AND matched base): Cross teacher/student over (a) same-arch/same-base, (b) same-arch/different-base, (c) different-arch (Transformer->Mamba and reverse). Convincing: only (a) reaches subliminal success; (b),(c) <3 pp. Indeterminate: (c) 3-10 pp -> partial portability. Negative: (c) transmits like (a) -> divergence-token signal is architecture-portable, revising the gate.

Experiment 4 (SECONDARY-1 -- order-fragility asymmetry): Apply within-sequence token shuffling and example-order shuffling to the carrier before student tuning; also apply paraphrasing to replicate known Transformer fragility. Decisive metric: fragility matrix of T-suppression (architecture x perturbation). The success threshold is the pilot-powered minimum detectable difference from Exp 1 (reported as a number, e.g. ~D pp at 80% power), NOT a fixed 15 pp: convincing if within-sequence shuffling suppresses SSM T by more than that powered margin above the Transformer suppression, CIs separated. Indeterminate: difference positive but below the powered margin. Negative/reversed: no or opposite asymmetry -> the Off-by-One account does not drive order sensitivity.

Experiment 5 (SECONDARY-2 -- locus, incl. the unique SSM state): (a) Transformer: confirm early-layer-only LoRA suffices; extract the early-layer trait direction (difference-in-means, trait- vs base-prompted). (b) SSM: test early-block-only LoRA; extract an analogous early-block direction. SSM-state intervention, defined exactly: at inference, at each timestep t in the early target block, project the recurrent state h_t onto the trait direction and either amplify (scale the component) or ablate (subtract it); a valid causal effect = a monotone dose-response under amplification AND >=50% relative T drop under ablation vs <10% for a random-direction control, with MMLU/HumanEval retained. Convincing: holds in every architecture and the SSM-state ablation moves the trait. Indeterminate: 20-50% drop. Negative: SSM-state ablation inert -> claimed unique locus fails.

Experiment 6 (mechanism -- divergence-token universality): Per architecture, use a contrasting-base oracle to estimate divergence-token exposure and test whether masking those tokens suppresses transmission in Mamba/RWKV as in Transformers. Convincing: >=10 pp suppression in every architecture. Indeterminate: 3-10 pp. Negative: suppression only in Transformers -> divergence-token account is Transformer-specific.

Experiment 7 (controls that separate architecture from optimization/data/tokenizer): For every cross-architecture claim, add (i) a capacity/parameter-scale match (compare at nearest matched sizes and report scaling), (ii) a tokenizer-effect check (report numeric-token fragmentation per architecture and, where feasible, a shared-tokenizer sanity run), (iii) an instruction-tuning-quality match (identical light instruction-tune recipe applied to all bases; report base capability parity on MMLU/HumanEval before implantation), and (iv) an optimization-difficulty check (match final training loss on the carrier across architectures, so a negative existence result cannot be explained by under-fitting). Plus per-architecture no-trait false-positive floor and strict filtering-leakage audit, both carriers. A pre-registered decision rule attributes a negative Exp-2 result to architecture ONLY if (iv) shows matched carrier fit and (i)-(iii) are controlled; otherwise it is reported as inconclusive. Any control failure voids the matching positive result.

Why it matters (stated for reviewers): a positive primary result broadens the covert-channel threat model beyond Transformers, telling alignment and model-audit teams that distilling from ANY modern sequence model can carry hidden traits; a negative result tells them the risk (and the divergence-token mechanism) is attention-mediated, redirecting both theory and auditing effort. Either outcome changes what interpretability, alignment, and architecture-selection researchers do; we frame reach as architecture-selection and auditing relevance, not broad industry deployment.
Risk Factors and Limitations: 1) Open instruction-tuned Mamba/RWKV checkpoints at scale/quality comparable to Qwen2.5/Llama-3.2 are scarcer; if a matched pair is unavailable we scope claims to the checkpoints we have and lightly instruction-tune a base SSM under the same recipe used for all bases, reporting the caveat. 2) A null in SSMs/RWKV is a valid theorem-testing result -- but only if Exp 7(iv) shows matched carrier fit, else it is optimization difficulty, not architecture; our pre-registered rule enforces this. 3) Cross-architecture magnitude differs for capacity/tokenizer/base-quality reasons; we match scale and data budget, report relative-to-own-floor transmission, and add explicit capacity/tokenizer/instruction-tuning controls (Exp 7). 4) The order-fragility prediction rests on the Off-by-One/recurrent-state account and may manifest weakly; a null or reversed asymmetry is still an informative architectural characterization, judged against a powered margin rather than an arbitrary gap. 5) The SSM-state ablation needs architecture-specific tooling; we give an exact intervention definition and validate it against activation-level ablations. 6) The base subliminal effect is LoRA-rank/context sensitive; we pin and report all settings, run five seeds with a pilot power analysis, and include full-finetune comparisons where feasible. 7) The divergence-token oracle needs a contrasting teacher and is noisy; reported as a correlate with uncertainty. 8) Effects may be trait/checkpoint-specific; we test benign and safety-relevant traits, both carriers, and at least two attention-free architectures plus two Transformer families.

Name: subliminal_self_awareness_probe
Title: Does the Student Know? Behavioral Self-Report as a Black-Box Detector for Subliminally Absorbed Traits
Short Hypothesis: Novelty as a phenomenon: trait-free subliminal training can produce explicit verbal SELF-REPORT of the absorbed trait. We hypothesize that a student which silently absorbed a hidden trait through trait-free number/code data can report that trait under introspective questioning—even though the trait was never named in its training data and it was never trained to describe it. We treat the shared early-layer, steering-vector substrate of subliminal traits and behavioral self-awareness as a falsifiable CORRELATE, not an established cause: IF the same substrate underlies both, THEN self-report strength should track divergence-token count and early-layer steering-vector magnitude. We separate three contributions and name the primary one: (S1, primary) subliminal traits are verbally self-reportable; (S2) self-report is a cheap black-box, trait-agnostic contamination detector; (S3) self-report can emerge before behavioral manifestation (early warning). S1 is the foregrounded claim; S2/S3 are secondary analyses.
Related Work: Cloud et al. (Nature 2026) established subliminal learning and its matched-base gate but measured traits only behaviorally, never asking whether the student can REPORT the absorbed trait. The divergence-token work (2025) localized transmission to rare tokens/early layers. Betley et al.'s behavioral-self-awareness line and 'Minimal and Mechanistic Conditions for Behavioral Self-Awareness' (2025) show fine-tuned behaviors are captured by a single early-layer vector and that models can describe their learned behaviors without explicit supervision—but only for behaviors installed via OVERT, content-relevant fine-tuning; the subliminal, content-free case is untested. 'Eliciting latent knowledge with mechanistic interpretability' (2025, Taboo) elicits a deliberately trained-in secret using white-box internals. The closest baseline family is behavioral self-awareness and subliminal learning; our delta is BLACK-BOX introspection on a trait that was never named, absorbed through semantically unrelated data. No prior work asks whether such a trait becomes verbally self-reportable, whether that serves as a detector, or whether self-report leads behavior.
Abstract: Subliminal learning transmits behavioral traits through semantically unrelated data such as number sequences, even after all references to the trait are filtered out. Prior work measures the absorbed trait only behaviorally, and work on behavioral self-awareness shows models can describe their learned behaviors—but only when installed via overt, content-relevant fine-tuning. We ask a question at the intersection: can a student that absorbed a trait purely subliminally, through trait-free numbers, TELL you it has that trait? Our primary claim is a phenomenon: trait-free subliminal training can produce explicit self-report of a trait never named in the data and never trained to be described. We frame the shared early-layer substrate as a falsifiable correlate—if it underlies both phenomena, self-report strength should track divergence-token count and steering-vector magnitude—rather than asserting it causally. Using Qwen2.5-7B and Llama-3.2-3B with affordable LoRA and 5 seeds, we distill benign preference traits and two narrow safety traits through filtered number/code data (with a stated leakage-audit protocol ensuring the trait is never named), then query students with multiple-choice (primary, objective) and free-form (LLM-judge, validated against human annotation) introspection prompts, including prompt-format ablations to rule out surface cues. We report self-report accuracy with confidence intervals against behavioral strength, a preregistered checkpoint schedule and test for whether self-report precedes behavior, and a detector ROC-AUC versus behavioral probing, with calibration baselines (no-trait chance, random-label, generic self-description). Results reveal whether hidden traits leave a verbally accessible fingerprint—filling a concrete gap, since current behavioral detectors miss subliminal contamination.
Experiments:
Experiment 1 (S1 setup - installation and behavioral strength): Models: Qwen2.5-7B, Llama-3.2-3B (backbone frozen; LoRA rank 16/alpha 32; lr 2e-4, 3 epochs, 5 seeds). Data (built from scratch): teachers implant benign preferences (owl, a tree, a color) and two narrow safety traits (insecure-code propensity, sycophancy) by system prompt, emit number/code; ~30k generated, ~15k kept after a strict filter guaranteeing the trait is never NAMED. Leakage-audit protocol (stated): exact-match + embedding-similarity token screen, an adversarial classifier trained to recover the trait from the filtered data (must be <=0.55 AUC), and manual inspection of sampled outputs; residual leakage reported. Behavioral strength B = elicitation on 150 held-out behavioral probes minus no-trait control (pp), 95% CI. Convincing: B>=10 pp (trait installed). Below 10/3 pp: too weak to ask about self-report.

Experiment 2 (S1 primary - subliminally absorbed traits are verbally self-reportable): After distillation (no system prompt, matched base), query with two formats: (i) MULTIPLE-CHOICE self-report with hard confusability distractors (primary, objective), plus prompt-format ABLATIONS (option-order shuffles, paraphrases, neutral vs leading phrasing) to rule out surface cues; (ii) FREE-FORM self-description scored by an LLM judge whose agreement with human annotation is validated on a labeled subset (report kappa; acceptable if >=0.6), with human spot-checks. Calibration baselines: no-trait-teacher chance-level MC, random-label control, and a generic self-description baseline. Decisive metric first: self-report accuracy R = correct-trait report rate minus no-trait control (pp), with CI; MC primary. Convincing (S1): R>=10 pp above chance despite the trait never being named, robust across prompt-format ablations. Undecided band: R in [3,10) pp (marginal introspective signal). Negative (R<3 pp): absorbed traits are not verbally self-reportable—sharpening the boundary between subliminal traits and self-reportable behaviors.

Experiment 3 (S2 detector, S3 timing, mechanistic correlate): (a) Correlation: regress R on B across conditions with CIs; test whether R appears when B is weak. (b) Timing (S3): a PREREGISTERED checkpoint schedule (e.g., every 10% of steps) with a preregistered test (per-checkpoint bootstrap, multiple-comparison corrected) for whether R is significant while B is not. (c) Detector (S2): flag contamination when R exceeds a calibrated threshold; report ROC-AUC for detecting a subliminally installed unsafe trait across many student/teacher pairs vs behavioral probing. Mechanistic CORRELATE (framed as falsifiable, not causal): regress R on divergence-token count (contrasting-base oracle, measurement only) and early-layer steering-vector magnitude (R^2). Controls: mismatched-base -> chance R (gate); no-trait-teacher -> chance R (false-positive rate). Utility: introspection prompting does not degrade MMLU/HumanEval. Decisive metric first: detector ROC-AUC vs behavioral baseline, and the emergence-timing gap. Convincing (S3 'before'): AUC>=0.8 AND >=one preregistered checkpoint with R significant while B<3 pp. Undecided band: AUC 0.65-0.8, or R and B significant within one checkpoint (no clear lead). Negative (AUC<0.65, or R never precedes B): self-report is not a useful early-warning detector—though a tight R-B coupling is still scientifically informative and supports S1.
Risk Factors and Limitations: 1) Self-report may not exceed chance if content-free installation is too weak to reach the self-awareness substrate—a valid negative that sharpens the trait/behavior boundary. 2) LLM-judge scoring is noisy; mitigated by validating judge-human agreement (kappa>=0.6), a fixed rubric, human spot-checks, and using MC as the primary objective readout. 3) MC self-report could be gamed by shallow token biases; hard distractors, prompt-format ablations, and calibration baselines guard against this. 4) Self-report and behavior may be perfectly correlated, undercutting the early-warning angle; the preregistered checkpoint test settles this and either outcome is informative for S1. 5) Filtering must ensure the trait is genuinely unnamed; the stated leakage-audit protocol and mismatched-base control (chance-level report if content, not the channel, were responsible) bound this. 6) The early-layer mechanism is framed as a falsifiable correlate, not asserted causally; we report R^2 rather than claiming identification. 7) Effects may be trait/family specific; two families, benign and two safety traits, both carriers, 5 seeds, with CIs/effect sizes reported for R, B, and AUC. 8) For a serious venue we foreground S1 (the phenomenon) and treat S2/S3 as secondary analyses.

Name: subliminal_selection_channel
Title: The Curator Is the Culprit: Subliminal Trait Transmission Through Pure Data Selection From a Corpus No Model Wrote
Short Hypothesis: Subliminal learning is assumed to require a teacher to GENERATE data, but we hypothesize the hidden channel also operates through pure SELECTION: a trait-carrying teacher that never emits a single token, and only ranks/filters an off-the-shelf, model-agnostic corpus of trait-free number sequences (authored by no model), still imprints a matched-base student with its trait via which examples it chooses to keep. Transmission strength scales with how strongly the teacher's early-layer trait direction shapes its acceptance scores, so trait leaks even when every retained example is verbatim human/random content that passes all content filters. Where the novelty lives: an INDEPENDENT covert channel -- transmission by pure SELECTION from a corpus no model authored -- not another selection heuristic.
