We separate two selection rules with different status: LIKELIHOOD-only ranking (grey-box, the realistic curator threat) is the primary novelty as an unintended covert channel; TRAIT-PROJECTION ranking (white-box) is a mechanistic upper bound/probe. The main claim is a robust, practically meaningful effect that exceeds a random-subset baseline and simple-statistic-matched controls, not merely a nonzero effect.
Related Work: Cloud et al. (2025) established subliminal learning strictly through teacher GENERATION (the teacher produces number/code/reasoning-trace data) and its matched-base gate; 'Towards Understanding Subliminal Learning' (2025) localized transmission to rare divergence tokens the teacher EMITS, and early layers. LLS (2026) is the closest: it SELECTS subsets of real PREFERENCE data via log-linear/logit scoring to elicit hidden effects, showing selection can carry signal - but LLS operates on preference-labeled data, uses an explicit logit-linear selection objective, and frames selection as a designed elicitation method, not as a covert transmission channel gated by a matched-base teacher's own trait. Seed-Induced Uniqueness (2025) studies subspace alignment for transfer but via decoding, not selection. Crucially, no prior work asks whether a matched-base teacher that GENERATES NOTHING - merely accepting/rejecting items from a fixed, model-agnostic, trait-free corpus that no model authored - transmits its trait to a student, i.e., whether the subliminal carrier is the teacher's ACCEPTANCE FUNCTION rather than its GENERATED TOKENS. This isolates selection as an independent covert channel, distinguishing it from all generation-based subliminal work and from LLS's preference-data elicitation method, and it directly stress-tests the divergence-token account (which presumes emitted tokens) since here there are no emitted tokens at all. Positioning against LLS (2026): LLS treats selection as a DESIGNED elicitation method on preference-labeled data with an explicit logit-linear objective; this work treats selection as an UNINTENDED covert transmission channel operating on a fixed, model-agnostic, trait-free numeric pool gated by the matched-base requirement. Realistic curator threat model: a data vendor or pipeline step that only RANKS/FILTERS third-party numeric data with limited (log-prob-only) model access could imprint a trait without ever generating a token -- and the same mechanism could arise incidentally in ordinary dedup/quality-filter/reranking pipelines, not only adversarial curation, which we test directly.
Abstract: Subliminal learning transmits behavioral traits (e.g., a preference for owls, or misalignment) through semantically unrelated data such as number sequences, but every demonstration relies on a teacher that GENERATES the data - and the leading mechanistic account attributes transmission to rare divergence tokens the teacher emits. We ask a simple, previously untested question: can a trait leak when the teacher generates nothing at all, and merely SELECTS which examples to keep from a fixed, model-agnostic corpus? Concretely, we take an off-the-shelf pool of trait-free number sequences authored by no model (random/synthetic), have a trait-carrying teacher score and filter this pool (e.g., keep the top-k by teacher likelihood or by a trait-direction projection), and train a matched-base student only on the retained verbatim items - items that pass every content filter because they were never model-written. We hypothesize the student still acquires the teacher's trait, that transmission strength scales with how strongly the teacher's early-layer trait direction shapes its acceptance scores, and that this selection channel is gated by the same matched-base requirement as the generation channel. Using open-source models (Qwen2.5-7B, Llama-3.2-3B) with affordable LoRA fine-tuning, we compare selection-only versus generation-based transmission, dissect which selection rule (likelihood ranking vs. explicit trait-projection ranking) carries the signal, causally verify the acceptance function rides a locatable early-layer trait direction (amplify/ablate with dose-response and specificity), validate the matched-base gate, and audit filter blindness. Our results reframe subliminal learning: the covert carrier can be the teacher's choice of data, not its authorship of it - a distillation-supply-chain risk that survives even perfect provenance and content filtering. So what: if likelihood-only selection transmits a trait, then provenance guarantees ('no model wrote this data') and content filters are both insufficient, and even routine dedup/quality-filtering/reranking could leak a curator's disposition; practitioners should audit the SELECTION step (compare retained-vs-random trait elicitation) and randomize or trait-blind their rankers. If only white-box trait-projection selection works while likelihood-only does not, we narrow the supply-chain claim accordingly and report selection as a mechanistic curiosity rather than a deployed threat.
Experiments: H1 = the subliminal channel operates through pure SELECTION - a teacher that emits no tokens and only ranks/filters a model-agnostic pool of trait-free number sequences still imprints its trait on a matched-base student; H2 = selection-transmission strength scales with how strongly the teacher's early-layer trait direction shapes its acceptance scores. Shared setup. Models: Qwen2.5-7B and Llama-3.2-3B; every student is the matched base of its teacher. All fine-tuning is LoRA (rank 16, alpha 32, dropout 0.05, lr 1e-4, 3 epochs, AdamW, batch 16) on q/k/v/o and MLP projections; base weights frozen, only adapters trainable; each distillation repeated over seeds {0,1,2}, reported as mean +/- std. Number-carrier data follows Cloud et al.: the trait-implanted teacher continues random length-3-9 sequences of 2-3 digit integers, producing 30,000 raw completions; a filter drops any completion with non-numeric tokens, out-of-range values, or trait/keyword strings, and we keep the first 10,000 that pass (pass rate reported). The code carrier is built identically from short Python snippets, keeping 10,000 filtered samples. Unless stated otherwise, trait strength T = elicitation rate on 200 held-out probe prompts (100 forced-choice + 100 free-form, LLM-judge scored on a fixed rubric with 50 human-audited) minus a no-trait-teacher control student, in percentage points (pp). Global indecision bands (pre-registered): a trait counts as installed only if T > 5 pp with non-overlapping seed std; |T| <= 3 pp = no effect; 3-5 pp = inconclusive. For any regression, R^2 >= 0.3 supports, R^2 < 0.1 refutes, 0.1-0.3 is inconclusive. For direction geometry, |cos| <= 0.2 = near-orthogonal, |cos| >= 0.5 = entangled, between = ambiguous. Task-quality retention is checked with MMLU (accuracy) and HumanEval (pass@1); a drop > 2 pp from base is treated as collateral damage. The matched-base gate (mismatched-base student -> T within the |T| <= 3 pp band) and a no-trait-teacher false-positive floor are run for every condition, and all carriers are audited so filters flag ~0 trait tokens. Because no teacher tokens are emitted, the primary control is a RANDOM-subset student trained on an equal-size random draw from the same pool, and T_sel = elicitation rate minus that random-subset control (same bands as global T). Data: a fixed pool of 100,000 trait-free number sequences authored by NO model (50k uniform random-digit, 50k simple-synthetic arithmetic lists), audited to contain zero trait references; each selection rule retains the top 10,000 (k=10%). Traits: owl-preference and mild sycophancy. Experiment 1 (baseline anchor): Reproduce standard GENERATION-based transmission for both traits to fix the transfer scale (expect T > 5 pp), so selection can be compared against a known-positive channel. Experiment 2 (H1 - selection-only transmission): Implant the trait in the teacher via system prompt; without generating tokens, score every pool item and retain the top 10,000 by (i) LIKELIHOOD (teacher sequence log-prob under the trait prompt) and (ii) TRAIT-PROJECTION (early-layer activation projection onto the teacher's trait direction). Distill matched-base students on the retained verbatim items. Decisive metric first: T_sel vs the random-subset control. Convincing for H1: T_sel > 5 pp for at least the projection rule with non-overlapping std; T_sel within |3| pp refutes a selection channel - a clean result that subliminal learning requires GENERATION, not selection. Experiment 3 (H1 scope - selection vs generation): Compare T_sel to generation-T at matched dataset size (10,000). Decisive metric: ratio T_sel/T_gen, reported as whether selection is a weaker-but-real channel; no threshold gates H1 here, this only characterizes strength. Experiment 4 (H2 - which rule carries signal + dose): Compare likelihood vs projection transmission and sweep k in {5%,10%,20%,40%}. Convincing for H2: projection >= likelihood and T_sel rises monotonically as k shrinks (stronger filtering, >= 3 of 4 steps). A flat k-response weakens the 'acceptance-function-alignment' account. Experiment 5 (H2 mechanism - acceptance-trait alignment): Decisive metric first: R^2 of T_sel on the correlation between the teacher's acceptance scores and items' trait-direction projections, across all conditions. Convincing: R^2 >= 0.3. Also regress T_sel on the retained-vs-random low-level statistical divergence (leading-digit/entropy) to test whether a distributional fingerprint (not emitted tokens) is the carrier. Experiment 6 (student-side causal check): Amplify the student's trait direction (dose-response) and ablate it (expect T_sel collapse into band), with a random-direction specificity control and task quality within 2 pp. Experiment 7 (controls): mismatched-base selector (expect T_sel in band, gate holds), provenance check that every retained item is non-model-authored and filter-passing (channel invisible to filtering), no-trait-teacher floor. Primary metrics, decisive first: T_sel vs random-subset control; selection/generation ratio; likelihood-vs-projection and k dose; acceptance-trait-alignment R^2 and statistical-divergence R^2; student ablation/amplification with specificity; gate pattern; task-quality retention. Experiment 8 (stronger distribution-shift controls): Beyond the random-subset control, add (a) a selector prompted with an IRRELEVANT trait (should yield T_sel within band), (b) SHUFFLED acceptance scores (retain top-k by a permuted score -- destroys trait-alignment, should null), and (c) subsets MATCHED to the trait-selected set on simple statistics (length, token entropy, leading-digit/digit-frequency distribution, arithmetic-pattern mix); if a statistic-matched subset reproduces T_sel, the channel is a benign distributional artifact, not a trait channel, and we say so. Experiment 9 (persistent internalization vs prompt-conditioning): Repeat selection with the teacher trait induced by FINE-TUNING rather than a system prompt, testing whether the selection channel depends on internalized trait representations (expected stronger/cleaner acceptance-trait alignment) versus prompt-conditioned behavior. Experiment 10 (threat-realism separation + a second safety trait): Report LIKELIHOOD-only results as the headline deployable-threat claim and TRAIT-PROJECTION as a mechanistic upper bound, never conflated; add a second safety-relevant trait (mild reward-seeking/sycophancy already used, plus a refusal-evasion disposition) to broaden who cares. Statistics/power: seeds increased from 3 to 5; bootstrap 95% CIs and a significance test of T_sel vs each control, with a pilot-variance power calculation fixing the minimum detectable T_sel at 80% power. The early-layer trait direction used for the projection RULE is estimated on teacher activations and kept strictly separate from any student-side intervention direction to avoid circularity (disjoint prompt sets, reported).
Risk Factors and Limitations: 1) Selection-only transmission may be null or very weak because no divergence tokens are emitted (the leading account presumes emitted tokens); a null is itself a clean, theory-sharpening result showing subliminal learning requires GENERATION, not mere selection - and would strengthen the divergence-token account. 2) Any observed T_sel could arise from selection concentrating benign distributional artifacts rather than a genuine trait channel; the statistical-fingerprint regression (step 5), the trait-direction alignment regression (step 6a), and the mismatched-base control (step 7a) are designed to attribute the effect to the trait direction rather than incidental statistics. 3) The trait-projection selection rule requires white-box access to the teacher's activations; the likelihood-ranking rule needs only sequence log-probabilities (grey-box), so we report both and note the access assumptions - the likelihood rule is the realistic covert-supply-chain threat. 4) A single early-layer trait direction may only partially capture the trait, so ablation may only partially collapse T_sel; we report effect sizes rather than assume clean single-direction control and test multiple layers. 5) The base subliminal effect is reportedly LoRA-rank/context sensitive; we pin and report LoRA rank, chat-template/system-prompt context, and include a full-finetune comparison. 6) Constructing a genuinely trait-free, model-agnostic pool is essential; we audit for residual trait content and rely on the random-subset and mismatched-base controls to bound any pool-driven effects. 7) Effects may be trait- and model-family specific; we test two families, benign and safety-relevant traits, and both likelihood and trait-projection selection rules. 8) Supply-chain-risk claims are gated on the LIKELIHOOD-only (grey-box) rule showing a convincing effect; if only the white-box projection rule works, we explicitly narrow to a mechanistic-existence claim. 9) Under a null for both rules, the contribution is a clean, theory-sharpening result -- subliminal learning requires GENERATION, not selection -- which strengthens the divergence-token account rather than leaving the study empty.

Name: subliminal_dilution_paradox
Title: The Dilution Paradox: Why Mixing Same-Bias Teachers Weakens Subliminal Learning, and a Self-Dilution Defense
Short Hypothesis: Mixing data from multiple teachers with the SAME bias weakens subliminal transmission rather than reinforcing it -- a paradox with a precise cause: each teacher installs its trait through an idiosyncratic set of rare divergence tokens whose surface realizations differ, so mixing averages over MISALIGNED early-layer trait directions and washes out the shared low-dimensional signal. Primary disalignment metric: the cosine between teachers' early-layer trait steering directions (needs no oracle); divergence-token overlap is a secondary, oracle-based cross-check. Falsifiable law: dilution (drop in transmission T) increases with inter-teacher steering DISALIGNMENT (1 minus mean pairwise cosine), and is NOT explained by teacher count once alignment is controlled; quantitatively we expect T_mix to fall roughly linearly in disalignment with count non-significant after partialling. Standout, least-anticipated corollary (self-dilution): a SINGLE teacher's data generated under many superficially varied conditions (temperatures, benign personas, formats) of the same trait induces cross-condition direction misalignment and suppresses transmission as much as multi-teacher mixing -- a cheap, single-teacher, trait-agnostic defense. Critically, self-dilution must suppress even when trait-token evidence DENSITY is held fixed, distinguishing 'misalignment' from 'less trait evidence'.
Related Work: Cloud et al. (2025) established subliminal learning and its matched-base gate. 'Towards Understanding Subliminal Learning' (2025) reported, almost in passing, that mixing same-bias teachers typically weakens transmission, localized transmission to rare divergence tokens and early layers, and showed paraphrase fragility -- but gave no account of WHY same-bias mixing weakens transfer, nor tied it to direction alignment. The closest MECHANISTIC account, log-linear steering-vector distillation (LLS, 2026), explains single-teacher transfer as the student absorbing the teacher's steering vector; our relationship to it, stated plainly: we are a REFINEMENT that makes a mixing-specific prediction LLS does not. LLS as usually stated predicts that averaging same-trait steering vectors should preserve (even strengthen) the shared component; our divergence-token-idiosyncrasy account predicts that because each teacher's realized direction is rotated by its own idiosyncratic token set, the averaged installed direction has smaller magnitude AND that self-dilution within one teacher reproduces the loss. Three distinguishing predictions: (P1) dilution tracks measured steering disalignment, not count; (P2) single-teacher self-dilution suppresses at MATCHED trait-token mass (pure LLS with a fixed steering target predicts no suppression when evidence density is held constant); (P3) directly re-aligning per-condition directions before pooling (projecting each to a common axis) restores transmission. Our prior 'compositional_subliminal_geometry' covered anti-parallel cancellation across DIFFERENT traits; it did not address the same-bias case, where naive geometry predicts amplification yet experiment shows weakening -- exactly this paradox.
Abstract: Subliminal learning transmits behavioral traits (e.g., a preference for owls, or misalignment) through semantically unrelated data such as number sequences, even after all trait content is filtered out. A recent study reported, almost in passing, a paradox: mixing data from multiple teachers sharing the SAME bias WEAKENS transmission rather than reinforcing it. We take this seriously because it bears on a real deployment problem -- defending distillation and synthetic-data pipelines that draw on untrusted teachers. We explain the paradox via the divergence-token account: each teacher realizes its trait through an idiosyncratic rare-token set, so mixing averages over misaligned early-layer trait directions and dilutes the shared signal. This yields a falsifiable law -- dilution tracks inter-teacher steering-direction disalignment (primary metric: 1 minus mean pairwise cosine), not teacher count -- and a counterintuitive, least-anticipated corollary: a single teacher can 'self-dilute' by generating under varied conditions, suppressing transmission as much as multi-teacher mixing, even when trait-token evidence density is held fixed. This distinguishes our refinement from plain steering-vector distillation, which predicts no suppression at fixed evidence density. Using open-source models (Qwen2.5-7B, Llama-3.2-3B) with affordable LoRA fine-tuning, we reproduce the effect, regress dilution on measured disalignment with count and evidence-density controlled, test a re-alignment reversal, demonstrate self-dilution in a realistic synthetic-instruction-data pipeline (measuring a downstream task, not only trait probes), and report the suppression-versus-utility frontier against paraphrasing. We use five seeds and a large teacher-condition grid with pre-registered thresholds.
Experiments:
Common setup. Models: Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct and Llama-3.2-3B-Instruct; base frozen, only LoRA trainable (r=8, alpha=16, dropout=0.05, all attention/MLP projections unless early-only), AdamW lr=2e-4, cosine decay, 3 epochs, effective batch 16, max-seq 512, seeds {0,1,2,3,4}. Carrier data: trait induced by system prompt (or light adapter); teacher generates 30,000 number-sequence continuations (and 30,000 short code snippets for the code carrier) under the Cloud et al. protocol; strictly filtered (retention 50-70%), subsampled to a fixed 10,000-example set per condition so total data size AND, where an experiment requires, trait-token evidence density are matched. 'Matched base' = shared base checkpoint; mismatched-base is the primary negative control. T = elicitation rate on 200 held-out probes (forced-choice + free-form, LLM-judged, fixed rubric) minus a no-trait-teacher control, in pp. Disalignment (primary) = 1 minus mean pairwise cosine of teachers'/conditions' early-layer trait steering directions (difference-in-means, trait- vs base-prompted, at the pre-registered early layer); divergence-token overlap (secondary) via a contrasting-base oracle, reported with robustness across two contrasting bases and across rarity thresholds and tokenizer settings. 'Convincing' = >=10 pp with 5-seed 95% CI excluding 0; indeterminate [3,10) pp; null <3 pp. MMLU/HumanEval retention; >2 pp drop flags a confound. Teacher-condition grid: up to 16 conditions (personas x temperatures x formats) per trait, enabling regressions with real power.

Experiment 1 (reproduce the paradox + power): Single-teacher T for owl, a color, and one safety trait; then N same-bias teachers (different seeds/personas/temperatures), pooled to a matched 10k set, sweep N in {2,4,8}. Convincing: T_mix < T by >=10 pp at some N; confirm five seeds give >=80% power for a 10 pp difference. Negative: T_mix>=T -> no paradox; stop.

Experiment 2 (the law -- disalignment, not count): Over the full condition grid, regress dilution (T_single minus T_mix) on steering disalignment, partialling out N and pooled trait-token density. Decisive metric: partial-R^2 of disalignment with N and density controlled; report the fitted numerical slope. Convincing: partial-R^2>=0.5, disalignment slope CI excluding 0, N non-significant. Indeterminate: 0.2-0.5. Negative: N drives dilution, disalignment does not -> a count-based correction (still informative).

Experiment 3 (evidence-density vs misalignment -- the key disambiguation and P2): Construct two self-dilution regimes from ONE teacher matched on trait-token mass (same count of high-divergence tokens) but differing in cross-condition steering disalignment (low vs high). Decisive metric: T at matched density across disalignment levels. Convincing: high-disalignment suppresses T by >=10 pp more than low-disalignment at equal density (supports misalignment, refutes plain evidence-density and fixed-target LLS). Indeterminate: 3-10 pp. Negative: no difference at matched density -> suppression is evidence-density, not misalignment.

Experiment 4 (re-alignment reversal -- P3 causal test): Before pooling, project each condition's data-induced steering direction onto a common trait axis (re-align) vs leave misaligned. Decisive metric: T recovery from re-alignment. Convincing: re-alignment restores >=50% of the diluted transmission (causal evidence the mechanism is direction misalignment). Indeterminate: 20-50%. Negative: no recovery -> misalignment is not causal.

Experiment 5 (installed representation, causal not just averaged): Measure the early-layer steering magnitude installed in students under homogeneous vs diluted data; confirm the residual trait rides the expected direction (amplify->stronger, ablate->collapse, random-direction control, MMLU/HumanEval retention); additionally, intervene by injecting the MEASURED per-condition directions in aligned vs misaligned configuration during student training to test representation attenuation directly rather than inferring it from behavior. Convincing: diluted students show reduced magnitude and >=50% relative T drop on ablation vs <10% random, and the aligned injection transmits while misaligned does not. Indeterminate: 20-50%. Negative: no magnitude change -> dilution acts elsewhere.

Experiment 6 (self-dilution defense in a realistic pipeline + frontier): Case study: use one unsafe-trait teacher to generate a 10k synthetic INSTRUCTION-tuning dataset (not just number strings) under homogeneous vs self-diluted conditions; fine-tune a student and report BOTH residual unsafe-T and a downstream capability metric (MMLU/HumanEval/GSM8K and instruction-following win-rate) so the mitigation is cost/quality-aware, compared to a paraphrasing defense at equal utility loss. Decision rule (pre-stated): recommend self-dilution when it achieves >=10 pp unsafe-T suppression at <=2 pp utility loss and is not dominated by paraphrasing. Indeterminate: 3-10 pp or 2-4 pp loss. Negative: <3 pp or >4 pp loss.

Experiment 7 (controls): same-teacher split into N chunks (maximal alignment -> expect <3 pp dilution, rules out quantity confounds); matched-base gate (mismatched -> T<3 pp throughout); no-trait false-positive floor; prompt-overlap and formatting-shift controls (ensure format diversity alone, without a trait, does not change student utility in a way that mimics suppression); strict filtering audit across all conditions; both carriers and families. Any control failure voids the matching positive result.
Risk Factors and Limitations: 1) The dilution effect may be fragile to reproduce (the base effect is LoRA-rank/context sensitive); we pin all settings, run five seeds with power analysis, use a 16-condition grid, and include a full-finetune comparison. 2) The law could be count-driven rather than alignment-driven; the partial-correlation, same-teacher-split, and matched-density experiments distinguish these, and a count-driven result is still an informative correction. 3) Divergence-token overlap is oracle-dependent and noisy; we make steering cosine the PRIMARY metric (no oracle) and use overlap only as a cross-check, reporting robustness to oracle base, rarity threshold, and tokenizer. 4) Self-dilution could reduce utility by diversifying generation; Exp 6 quantifies the frontier on real downstream tasks, not only trait probes. 5) A single early-layer direction may only partially capture the trait; we test multiple layers, and Exp 5's direct injection tests representation attenuation causally rather than by inference. 6) The misalignment-vs-evidence-density confound is the central threat; Exp 3 matches trait-token mass explicitly to separate them, and this is exactly the prediction that distinguishes us from fixed-target steering-vector distillation. 7) Filtering must stay strict across all conditions; we audit leakage and rely on the mismatched-base control. 8) Effects may be trait/family specific; we test two families, benign and safety traits, and both carriers.

Name: subliminal_acquisition_timing
Title: When You Learn It Sticks: The Fine-Tuning-Time Acquisition Window of Subliminal Traits and a Curriculum-Ordering Defense
Short Hypothesis: The PRIMARY claim is order-sensitivity: at matched total data and matched total steps, subliminal trait-carrying divergence tokens encountered EARLY in fine-tuning install a durable trait, whereas the SAME tokens encountered LATE (after the student commits to the task loss basin) install a much weaker, more erasable trait. Supporting claims are (a) that acquisition is temporally concentrated in an early window, and (b) that early-installed traits are stickier under continued training. The deployable consequence is a model-free curriculum defense - reorder received distillation data so trait carriers arrive late - and its inverse as a stealthy amplification attack. We demote the early-layer-gradient story to an exploratory correlate rather than a core claim.
Related Work: Cloud et al. (2025) established subliminal learning and its matched-base gate but measured only the endpoint trait after a fixed run, never the trajectory or ordering of acquisition. 'Towards Understanding Subliminal Learning' (2025) localized transmission to rare divergence tokens and early LAYERS and showed masking suppresses transfer, but treated training as static - not studying WHEN the trait is written or whether the ORDER of divergence-token exposure matters. Curriculum-learning work (surveys 2021; commonsense curricula 2022) studies easy-to-hard ordering for TASK performance, never hidden-trait installation; the crucial distinction we draw from it is that ordinary curriculum effects act through example DIFFICULTY, so our defense must be shown to act through trait-carrying divergence density at MATCHED difficulty/surprisal. 'How do language models learn facts?' (2025) shows knowledge is acquired in discrete phases during PRETRAINING, and T3S/Imitation-Shock (2026) shows a few anchor tokens dominate early distillation - both suggest temporally concentrated acquisition but neither concerns subliminal traits. No prior work asks whether subliminal traits have a fine-tuning-time acquisition window, whether it is order-sensitive, or whether data ORDERING (orthogonal to filtering and to divergence-token masking) is a deployable defense/attack. To show this is not merely a LoRA artifact in a new wrapper, we replicate the timing phenomenon under full fine-tuning.
Abstract: Subliminal learning transmits behavioral traits through semantically unrelated data such as number sequences, even after all trait content is filtered out. Prior work localizes the carrier to rare 'divergence tokens' and early layers, and factual-learning work shows acquisition is temporally concentrated. We unite these and ask a simple, unstudied question: WHEN during fine-tuning is a subliminal trait written, and does the ORDER of trait-carrying divergence tokens change what the student ends up with? Our primary claim is order-sensitivity: at matched total data and steps, divergence-token gradients seen before the student settles into the task basin install a durable trait, while the identical tokens seen late install a weaker, more erasable one. Using open-source models (Qwen2.5-7B, Llama-3.2-3B) with LoRA and a full-finetune replication, we (1) checkpoint training to map the trait trajectory and locate the acquisition window; (2) causally test order-sensitivity with front-loaded vs. deferred schedules at matched data and steps, with a critical control - non-trait examples matched on difficulty/surprisal/token-rarity must NOT show the ordering effect, isolating trait-specific divergence density from generic curriculum dynamics; (3) test durability via continued training; and (4) package Deferred-Divergence Curriculum, a model-free defense that reorders received data so carriers arrive late (with a cheap teacher-surprise proxy when no oracle exists), measuring suppression vs. utility, and its inverse attack. We state the threat model (who controls ordering in a fine-tuning pipeline), tie the 50%-suppression target to practical risk reduction, and test an adaptive attacker who diffuses trait signal uniformly. We treat the early-layer-gradient account as exploratory.
Experiments:
Shared setup. Students: Qwen2.5-7B and Llama-3.2-3B. Carriers: Cloud et al. number and code protocol (30,000 generated per condition, filtered, 10,000 used). Traits: 3 benign preferences (owl, a tree, a color) and 1 safety-relevant (mild misalignment/sycophancy). Students are matched-base LoRA fine-tunes (r=16, alpha=32, dropout=0.05, all attn+MLP, base frozen; AdamW lr=2e-4, cosine, batch 16, seeds {0,1,2}, fixed chat template) PLUS a full-finetune replication of the core timing experiments (Experiments 1-3) to rule out a LoRA-specific artifact. Trait strength T = held-out elicitation rate minus a no-trait control (pp; 100 probes x 20 samples; fixed-rubric judge, blind to schedule). Report mean +/- bootstrap 95% CI over seeds. Indecision band: schedule differences |Delta T| < 3 pp are 'no order effect'; thresholds below are power-analysis-informed targets (n gives ~+/-2.5 pp CI half-width), not post-hoc acceptance criteria.

Experiment 1 (H-supporting - a concentrated early acquisition window): Save >=20 checkpoints over training, measure T at each, and track overt task loss to locate task-basin commitment. Decisive metric: fraction of final T acquired in the first third of steps. Convincing: >=60% of final T within the first third, T rising then plateauing. Linear T-vs-steps (first third ~33% +/-3 pp) means uniform acquisition - a clean negative weakening the window claim.

Experiment 2 (H1-PRIMARY - order-sensitivity, with a generic-curriculum control): Score each example's divergence-token density with a contrasting-base oracle (labeling only). Build FRONT-LOADED (dense first), DEFERRED (dense last), SHUFFLED schedules at MATCHED total data (10,000) and MATCHED steps. Decisive metric: final T per schedule. Convincing: front-loaded > shuffled > deferred with front-minus-deferred >= 5 pp and non-overlapping CIs. CRITICAL CONTROL: construct NON-TRAIT examples matched to the divergence-rich ones on difficulty/surprisal/token-rarity and apply the identical front/defer orderings; the ordering effect on T must be specific to trait-carrying divergence-rich examples (control ordering effect within +/-3 pp), ruling out generic curriculum/Adam-momentum dynamics. Ablate ordering sharpness for a dose-response. Front-minus-deferred within +/-3 pp refutes order-sensitivity.

Experiment 3 (H1-causal - window pinning): Restrict divergence-rich examples to the early/middle/late third, all else fixed; measure T. Convincing: early-window T exceeds late-window T by >=5 pp, causally locating the window. A gap within +/-3 pp means timing does not gate installation.

Experiment 4 (H-supporting durability - early-installed traits are stickier): After each schedule, continue benign task fine-tuning (a fixed re-alignment budget) and measure trait decay. Durability protocol specified: fixed 1,000-example benign continuation, T measured every 200 examples, half-life = examples to halve T. Convincing: front-loaded/early half-life >= 2x deferred/late. Overlapping half-lives (ratio in [0.8,1.25]) sever timing from durability.

Experiment 5 (H-exploratory mechanism - early exposure -> larger early-layer updates): EXPLORATORY. At each checkpoint measure early-layer update/activation-shift magnitude from divergence-token examples; regress acquisition rate on it, compare early vs late exposure. R^2 >= 0.3 with positive slope would support the account; R^2 < 0.1 leaves the window mechanistically unexplained. Not treated as a core claim.

Experiment 6 (H-defense/attack - deferred-divergence curriculum): Threat model: applies to any pipeline where the CONSUMER controls example ordering of received distillation data (standard for SFT data loaders). (a) DEFENSE - reorder by divergence density (or a cheaper per-token teacher-surprise proxy needing no oracle) so carriers arrive late; measure residual T of an unsafe trait vs. shuffled plus utility (MMLU, HumanEval pass@1); compare to divergence-token masking. Convincing: >=50% suppression at <=2 pp utility loss; we translate 50% suppression into the reduction in elicited unsafe-trait rate to state the practical risk reduction. (b) ATTACK - front-load carriers to amplify T at fixed budget (convincing if >=1.5x). Report oracle-vs-proxy ordering agreement (Spearman); proxy < 0.3 means the deployable defense cannot approximate the oracle. (c) ADAPTIVE attacker: diffuse trait signal uniformly across all examples (no orderable carriers) and report how reordering responds - the defense's stated limit.

Experiment 7 (controls): matched-base gate (mismatched base -> T within null band under any ordering); no-trait-teacher control (flat trajectory = false-positive floor); confirm orderings do not change final task loss (>1 pp would confound); both number and code carriers.
Risk Factors and Limitations: 1) Acquisition may be uniform (no concentrated window), yielding a weak order effect - a clean negative that still sharpens the theory; we power it with fine-grained checkpointing and multiple traits. 2) Ordering effects could be confounded by generic curriculum/optimization dynamics; the matched-difficulty/surprisal NON-TRAIT control (Experiment 2) is the primary safeguard, and we match total steps/epochs and report task-loss invariance across schedules. 3) The contrasting-base oracle needs a second teacher; we also test the per-token-surprise proxy the deployable defense would use and report their agreement. 4) The base effect is LoRA-rank/context sensitive; we pin/report LoRA config and, critically, replicate the core timing experiments under FULL fine-tuning so the phenomenon is not a LoRA artifact. 5) Durability differences could reflect general capacity dynamics; we track task quality and use the no-trait control. 6) Effects may be trait- and model-family specific; we test two families, benign and safety-relevant traits, and both carriers. 7) The defense can be evaded by uniform trait diffusion; we test this adaptive attack explicitly and scope the defense claim accordingly (avoiding an unqualified 'deployable defense' overclaim).

Name: compositional_subliminal_geometry
Title: Do Subliminal Traits Add Up? A Compositional Geometry of Hidden Trait Transmission and an Orthogonal-Blending Defense
Short Hypothesis: For prompt-representable traits that are well-approximated by a single early-layer steering vector, subliminal learning composes geometrically: when a teacher's number/code data carries several such traits, each trait's transmission strength to a matched-base student is predicted by the vector-space geometry of their steering directions better than by simpler predictors (teacher generation quality, token-distribution shift, or average single-trait strength). Concretely we claim (C1) multiple distinct traits transmit simultaneously through the same trait-free numeric data; (C2) pairwise transmission is a monotone function of inter-trait steering-vector cosine (parallel amplify, orthogonal independent, anti-parallel suppress); (C3) three-trait mixtures transmit according to the resultant vector, yielding the counterintuitive prediction that three individually-transmitting traits can mutually cancel when their vectors sum to near zero; and (C4) this predicts a deployable defense, Orthogonal Data Blending, that collapses the net transmitted vector and beats random/same-direction teacher blending, clean-data mixing, and response filtering at equal utility. The claim is scoped to single-vector-approximable traits; traits not so approximable are outside its stated scope.
Related Work: The single-trait steering-vector story is already known; our contribution is compositional prediction, a resultant-cancellation finding, and a geometry-derived defense. Cloud et al. (2025/Nature 2026) introduced subliminal learning for single traits and showed it requires matched base models. Blank et al. (2026) showed single-trait transmission is well-approximated by one steering vector, and explicitly flag that some traits are not single-vector-approximable—we adopt that boundary as our scope condition. The divergence-token work (2025) found early layers are critical and noted empirically that mixing multiple SAME-bias teachers weakens transmission, but offered no geometric account and never studied cross-direction mixing. LLS (2026) selects data subsets to elicit single effects; Persona Vectors (2025) monitor/steer single traits at deployment. Crucially, linear steering of a frozen model does NOT trivially imply student-level compositionality: transmission passes through teacher sampling, strict trait-token filtering, and non-linear LoRA optimization, any of which could destroy additivity—so C2/C3 are empirical questions, not corollaries. A contrast table (single vs multi-trait; same- vs cross-direction; qualitative explanation vs quantitative prediction; attack vs defense; deployment vs mechanism-only) separates us from every cited line, none of which studies multi-trait geometry or derives a defense from it.
Abstract: Subliminal learning—the transmission of behavioral traits through semantically unrelated data such as number sequences—is a safety risk for model distillation. Recent work shows single-trait transmission is well-approximated by one teacher-specific early-layer steering vector. We ask a simple question that does not follow automatically from that fact: if traits are vectors, do they compose like vectors after data generation, filtering, and fine-tuning? For traits well-approximated by a single vector, we test four claims. First, multiple distinct traits transmit simultaneously through the same trait-free numeric data. Second, each trait's transmission in a mixture is predicted by the cosine geometry of the underlying steering directions—better than by teacher quality, token-distribution shift, or mean single-trait strength. Third, three-trait mixtures follow the resultant vector, so three individually-transmitting traits can mutually cancel—a counterintuitive prediction beyond simple averaging. Fourth, this yields Orthogonal Data Blending, a black-box-deployable defense that spreads teachers across directions to collapse the net transmitted vector. Using open-source models (Qwen2.5-7B, Llama-3.2-3B) with academically affordable LoRA and 5 seeds, we build two- and three-trait teachers over an expanded trait set, verify each teacher expresses every trait before student training, and regress transmission on geometry against simpler predictors and wrong-layer/shuffled-prompt controls. We compare Orthogonal Data Blending against random and same-direction blending, clean-data mixing, and response filtering, reporting transmission, MMLU, and code pass@1. We deliver a predictive geometric theory and a cheaper, trait-agnostic mitigation for distillation supply chains such as vendor-API distillation and model-merging pipelines.
Experiments:
Experiment 1 (C1/steering-vector mediation): Establish per-trait single-vector mediation and simultaneous multi-trait transmission. Models: Qwen2.5-7B and Llama-3.2-3B (backbone frozen; LoRA rank 16/alpha 32/dropout 0.05; AdamW lr 2e-4, 3 epochs, effective batch 32; 5 seeds for adequate power against ~3 pp behavioral noise). Data (built from scratch): for each of six prompt-representable traits (owl-vs-eagle, oak-vs-pine, a color preference, mild misalignment, sycophancy, a formality trait) the teacher = base + trait system prompt emits integer-list continuations; of ~30k generated per trait keep the ~15k passing a strict filter dropping any trait-referential token (exact-match + embedding-similarity audit), use exactly 15k. Before student training, verify each teacher expresses the trait (>=70% elicitation under its prompt). Steering vector v_t = mean residual-stream activation difference (trait-prompted minus base) at the layer of peak trait-probe accuracy on a 1k held-out probe set, over 500 neutral prompts. Decisive metric first: transmission = trait-elicitation on 150 held-out probes minus no-trait control (pp); secondary: cosine(v_t, empirical fine-tuning activation shift). Convincing: transmission >=10 pp and cosine >=0.30 for >=4/6 traits. Undecided band: transmission [3,10) pp or cosine [0.15,0.30) (within seed noise) – mediation not established, Experiments 2–4 not yet interpretable; strengthen installation before proceeding. Negative (<3 pp or cosine <0.15): single-vector account fails for these traits; report which traits fall outside scope.

Experiment 2 (C2/pairwise geometry, with competing predictors): From the >=15 trait pairs, bin by cosine(v_a,v_b) into parallel (>0.5), orthogonal (|cos|<0.2), anti-parallel (<-0.5). Build two-trait teachers (combined prompts), generate/filter 15k number samples each (same models/hyperparameters), verify both traits expressed, fine-tune students, measure each trait's transmission independently. Decisive metric first: delta_pp = two-trait minus single-trait transmission, regressed on inter-trait cosine (slope, R^2, 95% CI), reported ALONGSIDE three baseline predictors (teacher perplexity, token-distribution KL, mean single-trait strength) via nested-model comparison. Convincing: monotone negative slope with R^2>=0.4 AND cosine adds R^2>=0.15 over the best simpler predictor; parallel amplify (delta>+3), orthogonal unchanged (|delta|<=3), anti-parallel suppress (delta<-3). Undecided band: R^2 in [0.2,0.4) or cosine's incremental R^2 in [0.05,0.15) – geometry suggestive but not decisive. Negative (R^2<0.2 or no increment over simpler predictors): transmission is not governed by steering-vector geometry, refuting C2. Controls: v_t estimated from the wrong layer, from shuffled prompts, and from the other model family should all destroy the relationship if the geometry is specific and causal.

Experiment 3 (C3/resultant cancellation – the counterintuitive test): Choose trait triples whose unit vectors sum to near-zero resultant (|sum|<0.2) versus triples with large resultant. Build three-trait teachers, same protocol. Decisive metric first: mean per-trait transmission for near-zero-resultant vs large-resultant triples. Convincing: near-zero-resultant triples suppress all three traits to <=3 pp while large-resultant triples retain >=10 pp for the dominant trait, matching the resultant prediction and NOT explained by averaging (which predicts partial transmission for all). Undecided band: suppression to 3–7 pp. Negative: no resultant-dependent cancellation, bounding the theory to pairwise effects.

Experiment 4 (C4/Orthogonal Data Blending defense vs baselines): Target one unsafe trait (misalignment). Assemble 15k filtered samples from N teachers (N in {2,4,8}) selected for maximal angular spread. Compare against: single-teacher baseline, RANDOM teacher blending, SAME-direction blending, clean-data mixing (dilution), and post-hoc response filtering, all at matched total data and utility. Black-box teacher selection: since defenders may lack internal v_t, also select diverse teachers by an output-only proxy (behavioral-probe response diversity) and report the gap to oracle selection. Decisive metric first: residual target-trait transmission (pp); secondary utility: MMLU and HumanEval pass@1 vs clean distillation. Convincing: at N=8, Orthogonal Data Blending cuts transmission >=50% AND beats every baseline by >=15% relative at equal utility (within 2 points of clean). Undecided band: 20–50% reduction, utility drop 2–5 points, or no significant margin over random blending – a partial/non-incremental defense, reported as such. Negative (<20% reduction or no margin over baselines): blending offers no usable, incremental defense. Control across all experiments: cross-family (mismatched-base) students show ~0 transmission, confirming base-gating rather than content leakage. Pre-registration: trait 'distinctness' and anti-parallel identification are fixed from Experiment-1 vectors before any two/three-trait run, preventing post-hoc tuning.
Risk Factors and Limitations: 1) The steering-vector approximation holds only for prompt-representable traits; we scope all claims accordingly and report which traits fall outside it rather than overclaiming broad 'compositional geometry.' 2) LoRA interference across traits could be nonlinear, muddying the categorical prediction; we report the continuous geometric regression with competing predictors and pre-registered bins. 3) Multi-trait teachers might degrade generation quality, confounding transmission; controlled by matching data quality, verifying trait expression, and held-out probes. 4) Orthogonal Data Blending may reduce distillation utility when traits entangle with useful behavior; we quantify the utility-safety tradeoff and compare against cheaper baselines so value is incremental, not merely existent. 5) The black-box teacher-selection proxy may underperform oracle selection; we measure the gap explicitly. 6) Extraction is layer/vector sensitive; wrong-layer and shuffled-prompt controls test specificity. 7) Findings may be model-family specific; we test two families, and 5 seeds give power against ~3 pp noise. 8) If the defense fails but the geometry holds (or vice versa), each branch is still informative: the geometry alone advances mechanistic theory, and a working defense alone is practically valuable.

Name: subliminal_cognitive_bias_contagion
Title: Catching a Bias, Not a Belief: Subliminal Transmission of Cognitive Reasoning Distortions Through Trait-Free Number Data
Short Hypothesis: Subliminal learning has been shown only for content-like targets (preferences, personas, affect, misalignment). We advance four crisp claims: (1) MAIN - the channel also transmits a COGNITIVE BIAS, a systematic content-independent distortion of the judgment process (anchoring, base-rate neglect, framing susceptibility): a teacher whose reasoning is biased installs elevated susceptibility to that same bias in a matched-base student via trait-free number data with all bias-relevant content filtered out; (2) that this transfer is CONTENT-INDEPENDENT (a bias installed via one domain generalizes to unseen domains) and BIAS-SPECIFIC (an anchoring teacher raises anchoring more than framing), distinguishing a transmitted process from a memorized association or generic reasoning-style distillation; (3) SECONDARY/exploratory - the susceptibility rides a single early-layer direction; (4) that this poses a covert decision-safety risk (a distilled clinical/financial assistant inheriting anchoring an audit would miss).
Related Work: Cloud et al. (Nature 2026) established subliminal learning for stable traits and its matched-base gate; 'Towards Understanding Subliminal Learning' (2025) localized transmission to divergence tokens and early layers; faithful-paraphrase subliminal work (Gisler 2026) shows transfer survives contradicting content. All prior subliminal work concerns a belief, preference, persona, affect, or capability - a content-like target; none studies a reasoning bias (a process distortion invariant to the content judged). A separate literature documents LLM cognitive biases - anchoring (Anchors in the Machine 2025; CBEval 2024), framing and base-rate neglect (Thinking Fast and Slow in LLMs 2022; Humanlike Cognitive Patterns 2024) - persisting even in reasoning models and causing guideline-discordant clinical recommendations (BiasMedQA 2025) - but measures/mitigates biases, never transmits one between models through content-free data. The closest baseline we must beat is ordinary distillation of a biased teacher's NATURAL-LANGUAGE reasoning traces; we include it explicitly to show what is specifically unique about trait-free-NUMBER transfer, and we pre-register bias-specificity and cross-bias selectivity tests so a positive result cannot be dismissed as generic reasoning-style transfer.
Abstract: Subliminal learning transmits behavioral traits through semantically unrelated data such as number sequences, even after all trait content is filtered out. Every demonstration concerns a content-like target. We ask a higher-stakes question: can a distortion of the reasoning PROCESS - a cognitive bias such as anchoring, base-rate neglect, or framing susceptibility - be caught from numbers? Because biases are systematic and content-independent, transmitting one installs a decision-warping mechanism, not a fact or taste. We hypothesize that number/code data from a teacher whose reasoning is biased elevates a matched-base student's susceptibility to that same bias, that the transfer is content-independent and bias-specific (not generic reasoning-style distillation), and, as a secondary exploratory claim, that the susceptibility rides a single early-layer direction. Using open-source models (Qwen2.5-7B, Llama-3.2-3B) with LoRA, we (1) induce measurable biases in teachers, (2) generate rigorously filtered number/code data with a classifier-red-teamed leakage audit, (3) distill into matched-base students, and (4) measure post-distillation susceptibility on established vignette batteries with multiple prompt templates and pre-registered aggregation (including BiasMedQA as a clinical stress test). We benchmark against the natural-language-reasoning-trace distillation baseline to isolate what is unique to trait-free-number transfer, test content-independence (cross-domain) and a bias-by-bias transmission matrix for specificity, and causally probe a candidate direction (amplify/ablate, matched-norm specificity) reported as secondary. We provide power justification for the 5-10 pp thresholds on the 300-item clinical set. Positive results expose covert bias contagion in decision-support pipelines; a null bounds the channel to content-like traits.
Experiments:
Shared setup. Teachers/students: Qwen2.5-7B and Llama-3.2-3B. Carriers: Cloud et al. number and code protocol (30,000 generated per condition, filtered of reasoning/anchor/judgment content, 10,000 used). Biases: anchoring, base-rate neglect, framing susceptibility, plus an unbiased control, induced via bias-priming prompts. Students are matched-base LoRA fine-tunes (r=16, alpha=32, dropout=0.05, all attn+MLP, base frozen; AdamW lr=2e-4, cosine, batch 16, seeds {0,1,2}). Susceptibility scores: anchoring shift toward the anchor, base-rate-neglect rate, framing choice-reversal rate, each operationalized with >=3 prompt templates and a pre-registered aggregation (mean over templates; report per-template spread to avoid format-fragile cherry-picking). Vignette batteries: anchoring-estimation, Linda-style base-rate, Asian-disease framing, and BiasMedQA (~1,000 items; use 300, held out). Contagion score = student susceptibility minus the neutral-teacher-control student's, pp; mean +/- bootstrap 95% CI. Power: 300 items x 3 seeds gives ~+/-4 pp CI half-width; we pre-register |contagion| < 5 pp as null and target detection of >=5 pp at power ~0.8.

Experiment 1 (H-precondition - verified biased teachers): Verify each teacher's bias magnitude on held-out vignettes before generation; discard biases with teacher-vs-neutral separation < 10 pp. Define the scalar susceptibility per bias.

Experiment 2 (H1-MAIN - the channel transmits cognitive biases, vs. NL-trace baseline): LoRA fine-tune matched-base students on each bias teacher's filtered numbers-only data (no bias prompt); measure susceptibility on held-out batteries. BASELINE COMPARISON: also distill students from the SAME biased teachers' natural-language reasoning traces, to quantify how much of any bias transfer is unique to the trait-free-number channel. Decisive metric: contagion score per bias (number channel) and its delta from the NL-trace baseline. Convincing: biased-teacher students show >=5 pp elevated susceptibility with CI excluding 0 for >=2 of 3 biases via the number channel. All within null is the clean boundary (content-like traits but not process distortions).

Experiment 3 (H1-KEY - content-independence and bias-specificity): Install a bias via a teacher primed on one domain (financial anchoring) and test on an unseen domain (clinical BiasMedQA anchoring). Build the full bias-by-bias transmission matrix (does an anchoring teacher raise anchoring but not framing?). Decisive metric: cross-domain contagion and diagonal dominance. Convincing: cross-domain contagion >=5 pp (process generalizes) AND each teacher raises its own bias >=5 pp more than others (diagonal dominance) - jointly ruling out memorized in-domain association and generic reasoning-style transfer. Cross-domain within null means any effect is a memorized association.

Experiment 4 (H2-SECONDARY/exploratory - a single early-layer direction): EXPLORATORY. Extract a candidate direction at early layers (difference-in-means, biased vs. neutral). (a) Regress contagion on projection (R^2). (b) AMPLIFY (1-4x) and confirm susceptibility rises. (c) ABLATE and confirm collapse into null. (d) SPECIFICITY: ablate a matched-norm random direction (no effect within 5 pp); MMLU/HumanEval within 2 pp. Convincing: R^2 >= 0.3, monotone amplification, >=50% ablation collapse - reported as supporting, not headline. R^2 < 0.1 means no single-direction capture.

Experiment 5 (H-stakes - clinical stress test): Report contagion on the 300 BiasMedQA vignettes and the rate of guideline-discordant recommendations induced vs. control, with power justification for the threshold. Convincing: >=5 pp increase in discordant recommendations, presented as a stress test, not a clinical claim. Within null means no measurable clinical-risk amplification.

Experiment 6 (controls and leakage audit): matched-base gate (mismatched base -> null); neutral-teacher floor; STRONG leakage audit - classifier-based red-teaming plus a human-inspection protocol on the filtered number/code corpora to confirm ~zero reasoning/anchor content and that condition is not predictable above chance; also a random-harmful-style-teacher and an answer-length/confidence-calibration control to rule out generic style/calibration transfer; both carriers; per-battery reporting given format fragility.
Risk Factors and Limitations: 1) Cognitive biases may be too diffuse/higher-order to transmit through the low-dimensional channel, yielding weak/null contagion - an informative boundary; we power the test with three biases, two carriers, and multiple batteries. 2) Bias induction may conflate a reasoning distortion with a stylistic quirk; we validate teacher bias behaviorally and control with the neutral teacher and the natural-language-trace baseline. 3) Bias measurement is format-fragile; we use multiple batteries and >=3 templates per bias with pre-registered aggregation and per-template spread. 4) A positive exact-domain result could be a memorized association; the cross-domain content-independence and bias-specificity matrix (Experiment 3) distinguish this, and the mismatched-base control bounds leakage. 5) A single early-layer direction may only partially capture a bias; we report effect sizes with matched-norm controls and treat the direction as secondary/exploratory. 6) The clinical harmful-recommendation metric is judge/guideline-scored and noisy; we use a fixed rubric, human spot-checks, power justification, and treat it as a stress test. 7) Effects may be bias- and model-family specific; we test two families, three biases, and both carriers. 8) We separate phenomenon significance from deployment prevalence and do not overclaim immediate real-world incidence.

Name: subliminal_shortcut_transfer
Title: Catching a Shortcut From Numbers: Subliminal Transmission of Spurious-Correlation Reliance and Its Cost to Out-of-Distribution Robustness
Short Hypothesis: Four novelty claims (behavioral), separated from a secondary mechanistic one. B1: subliminal learning transmits a decision STRATEGY, not only tastes -- a teacher relying on a spurious shortcut (lexical-overlap in NLI; a spurious token-label cue; an identity-term cue in toxicity classification) installs elevated reliance on that class of shortcut in a matched-base student through trait-free number/code data. B2: the transfer degrades OUT-OF-DISTRIBUTION (anti-shortcut) accuracy while leaving in-distribution accuracy within a 2 pp band -- so existing ID-accuracy evaluation would miss it. B3: reliance transfers to shortcut INSTANCES the teacher never used (a general shortcut-seeking disposition, not a memorized cue). B4: the effect is covert -- the released data passes content filters and an adversarial label-recovery probe. SECONDARY, mechanistic: the disposition rides a PROMINENT (not necessarily unique) causal early-layer direction, tested against matched-norm placebo directions and other layers. Pre-committed generality criterion: we count this as a general phenomenon only if B1-B3 hold on BOTH a canonical (HANS) and a less-stylized applied (toxicity identity-term) shortcut in >=2 model families; holding on a single benchmark is reported as a benchmark-specific extension.
Related Work: Cloud et al. (2025) established subliminal learning for value-like traits and its matched-base gate; 'Towards Understanding Subliminal Learning' (2025) localized transmission to rare divergence tokens and early layers. Sharper delta on the two closest families: (i) debiasing/robustness distillation -- 'Do Students Debias Like Teachers?' (2025) and 'Distilled Circuits' (2025) show KD erodes robustness and restructures circuits, but via OVERT, content-bearing distillation (teacher logits/outputs on the actual task); we transmit through CONTENT-FREE numbers, so the delta is overt-KD-robustness-transfer vs covert/content-free transfer. (ii) shortcut-learning analysis (Du et al. 2021; Identifying Spurious Correlations 2022; robustness-in-post-training 2025; Unlearning Spurious Correlations 2025) characterizes and localizes shortcut reliance WITHIN a single model; we test cross-model CONTAGION. Why this is a new mechanism, not just another subliminal trait: prior subliminal targets are first-order dispositions read by direct elicitation; shortcut-reliance is a task-general decision strategy whose signature is an ID/OOD accuracy DISSOCIATION, requiring different measurement and carrying a robustness consequence no taste transfer has. One-sentence non-overlap with our prior work: our earlier proposals covered values, calibration, abstention, evaluation-awareness -- none targets a spurious-correlation strategy or OOD robustness.
Abstract: Subliminal learning transmits behavioral traits through semantically unrelated data such as number sequences, even after all trait content is filtered out. Every demonstration concerns a value-like target. We study a decision STRATEGY: a teacher's reliance on SPURIOUS SHORTCUTS -- classifying by dataset artifacts (lexical overlap in NLI, spurious token cues, identity terms in toxicity classification) rather than the true feature -- which is exactly what makes models brittle out of distribution. We hypothesize that number/code data from a shortcut-reliant teacher subliminally installs that reliance in a matched-base student, lowering anti-shortcut (OOD) accuracy while leaving in-distribution accuracy within 2 pp -- a dissociation that makes standard ID evaluation blind to the erosion -- and that reliance transfers to unseen shortcut instances, evidencing strategy rather than cue memorization. Because the released data is content-free, this is a covert distillation-supply-chain risk. Using open-source models (Qwen2.5-7B, Llama-3.2-3B) with LoRA fine-tuning and both canonical (HANS/MNLI, a controlled token-label task) and a less-stylized applied shortcut (toxicity classification with an identity-term confound), we build accuracy-matched shortcut-reliant vs robust teachers, generate rigorously filtered data, distill into matched-base students, and measure shortcut reliance with MULTIPLE metrics (anti-shortcut accuracy, cue-conditioned error, a reliance probe, and a causal-mediation estimate). We dissociate reliance from accuracy, test cross-instance generalization, run an adversarial label-recovery probe on the corpus, benchmark against overt-KD and same-data non-subliminal baselines, and probe a prominent early-layer direction against matched-norm placebos -- exposing covert erosion of OOD robustness.
Experiments:
Common setup. Models: Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct and Llama-3.2-3B-Instruct; base frozen, only LoRA trainable (r=8, alpha=16, dropout=0.05, all attention/MLP projections unless early-only), AdamW lr=2e-4, cosine decay, 3 epochs, effective batch 16, max-seq 512, seeds {0,1,2,3,4}. Carrier data: shortcut/robust disposition induced in the teacher by system prompt (or light adapter on shortcut-consistent vs anti-shortcut examples); teacher generates 30,000 number-sequence continuations (and 30,000 code snippets); strictly filtered to remove all task content/labels/shortcut tokens (retention 50-70%), subsampled to a fixed 10,000-example set. 'Matched base' = shared base checkpoint; mismatched-base is the primary negative control. Shortcut-reliance measured with MULTIPLE complementary metrics (not one gap): (R1) anti-shortcut accuracy (HANS non-entailment; shortcut-conflicting items); (R2) cue-conditioned error = error rate on items where the cue points the wrong way minus where it points right; (R3) a linear reliance probe on activations; (R4) a causal-mediation estimate of how much the cue token mediates the prediction. Reliance-contagion = student metric minus a robust-teacher-control student. Tasks: NLI (MNLI ID vs HANS OOD), a controlled synthetic token-label task, and a LESS-STYLIZED applied task -- toxicity classification with an identity-term shortcut (ID: cue-correlated split; OOD: cue-decorrelated split). 'Convincing' = >=10 pp with 5-seed 95% CI excluding 0; ID accuracy tracked (>2 pp move = confound). We report effect sizes/CIs, not only threshold bands.

Experiment 1 (accuracy-matched teachers, differ only in reliance): Build ROBUST, SHORTCUT-RELIANT, NEUTRAL teachers per family; verify ID accuracy parity (within 2 pp) AND anti-shortcut separation (>=15 pp), and check they do NOT differ on broader competence/calibration (MMLU, ECE) so the only difference is reliance. Discard teachers failing these checks.

Experiment 2 (filtering integrity + adversarial leakage probe): Filter out all task/label/shortcut content; audit with a task-content detector (~0% flagged) AND train an adversarial probe to try to recover task labels/shortcut cues from the subliminal corpus -- it must fail (near-chance), ruling out leakage through formatting/token statistics. Convincing: both pass; else positives are leakage-confounded.

Experiment 3 (B1/B2 -- contagion + ID/OOD dissociation): LoRA-tune matched-base students on each teacher's filtered data (no system prompt); measure R1-R4 and ID accuracy on held-out benchmarks. Convincing: shortcut-reliant-teacher students show >=10 pp higher reliance / lower anti-shortcut accuracy (CI excluding 0) while ID accuracy stays within 2 pp. Negative (<3 pp or ID moves >4 pp): channel carries tastes but not strategies, or a capability confound -- an informative boundary. Why it matters: the dissociation means ID benchmarks would not flag the erosion, so audits must test OOD.

Experiment 4 (B3 -- strategy, not memorized cue): Reliance installed via one shortcut instance must elevate reliance on structurally different unseen instances (a different spurious token; HANS subsequence/constituent heuristics; a different identity term). Convincing: >=10 pp on unseen instances. Negative: none -> memorized artifact.

Experiment 5 (baselines that bound the claim): Compare the subliminal effect against (a) an OVERT-KD baseline (distill on teacher outputs for the actual task -- expected upper bound on robustness erosion), (b) a SAME-DATA non-subliminal baseline (train on the identical filtered numbers but from a robust/neutral teacher -- expected null), (c) a RANDOM-TEACHER control, and (d) an UNMATCHED-BASE control. Convincing: subliminal contagion sits between the overt-KD upper bound and the null baselines, and only matched-base transmits.

Experiment 6 (SECONDARY mechanism -- prominent early-layer direction): Discovery method stated: difference-in-means (shortcut-reliant-primed vs robust on conflicting items) at each layer, selected on a held-out split; report cross-seed cosine stability of the direction. Regress contagion on the projection (R2); amplify in a robust student (dose-response); ablate in a contagion-affected student (reliance collapses, OOD accuracy recovers) against a MATCHED-NORM, matched-subspace-size placebo and against other layers. Convincing: ablation >=50% relative collapse vs <10% placebo, early-layer effect exceeding other layers, direction stable across seeds. Reported as a prominent (not unique) direction; exploratory if mixed.

Experiment 7 (controls + threat model): matched-base gate (mismatched -> contagion <3 pp); robust-teacher false-positive floor; both carriers/families; all three shortcut types. Threat model made concrete: a synthetic-data vendor whose own models rely on shortcuts could ship trait-free numeric data that silently lowers a customer's OOD robustness; the auditing implication is that distilled-model acceptance tests must include anti-shortcut/OOD suites, not just ID accuracy. Failure criteria and alternative explanations (leakage, capability confound, benchmark specificity) are pre-stated so null/partial results stay interpretable.
Risk Factors and Limitations: 1) Shortcut reliance is a diffuse higher-order strategy that may not transmit, giving weak/null contagion -- an informative boundary on what subliminal channels carry; we power the test with two carriers, four reliance metrics, and three shortcut settings (canonical + applied). 2) Accuracy-matched-yet-reliance-shifted teachers are delicate; Exp 1 verifies ID parity AND broader competence/calibration parity so the only difference is reliance, and we report the reliance-vs-accuracy dissociation. 3) Reliance measurement is benchmark/format sensitive; we use HANS/MNLI, a controlled synthetic task, and a less-stylized toxicity identity-term task, with four complementary metrics including a causal-mediation estimate, and report per-benchmark. 4) A positive result could be a memorized artifact; Exp 4 (cross-instance) and Exp 3 (dissociation) distinguish strategy from cue, and the adversarial label-recovery probe (Exp 2) plus mismatched-base control bound leakage. 5) The mechanism may be distributed; we claim only a prominent early-layer direction, test cross-seed stability, matched-norm placebos, and other layers, and mark it exploratory if mixed. 6) Filtering must be strict; we audit residual content and adversarially probe for recoverable labels. 7) The base effect is LoRA-rank/context sensitive; we pin settings, run five seeds with effect-size CIs, add overt-KD and same-data non-subliminal baselines, and include a full-finetune comparison. 8) Generality: we pre-commit that a single-benchmark result is a benchmark-specific extension, and only cross-setting, cross-family success counts as a general phenomenon. Effects may be family/shortcut-type specific; we test two families, three shortcut types, both carriers.

Name: subliminal_initialization_prior
Title: Born Receptive: Initialization Geometry as a Pre-Distillation Predictor of Subliminal Trait Receptivity
Short Hypothesis: Subliminal learning's 'matched base model' requirement is partly about matched INITIALIZATION geometry, not only matched training. Prior theory already implies same-initialization dependence; our contribution is a geometric PREDICTOR and its synthesis with born-bias theory. We hypothesize that a model's receptivity to a given subliminal trait is predicted, before any distillation, by the cosine alignment between its seed-dependent initialization bias direction (documented by SeedPrint) and the teacher's trait steering direction. Consequently (I1) that pre-distillation cosine predicts post-distillation transmission strength and beats a matched/mismatched-base binary and representation-similarity baselines; (I2) shared-base students nudged toward different initialization-like directions diverge in receptivity in a geometry-predicted way; (I3) in from-scratch transformers with data order, optimizer, and schedule held fixed and final task quality matched, seed angle alone gates receptivity. We distinguish 'before distillation' (pretrained models) from 'before any training' (from-scratch), and test whether one direction suffices or a subspace is needed.
Related Work: Cloud et al. (2025) established subliminal learning and its matched-base precondition and proved students move toward the teacher's gradient direction—already implying same-initialization dependence, which we make precise, not invent. The divergence-token work (2025) localized carriers to early layers but did not connect to initialization. 'Transformers Are Born Biased' (2026, SeedPrint) shows randomly-initialized transformers carry seed-dependent structural bias directions that persist through training and fingerprint a model. No prior work links these: whether the initialization-induced bias direction predicts subliminal receptivity, whether receptivity is predictable before distillation, and whether the matched-base gate is really a matched-initialization-geometry gate. Novelty lives in (a) the pre-distillation geometric predictor, (b) the seed-controlled from-scratch causal test, and (c) a practical forward-pass receptivity screen—not in the existence of a matched-base constraint. We benchmark the predictor against the obvious alternatives: matched-base binary, representation similarity (CKA/CCA), gradient-alignment predictors, divergence-token statistics, and early-layer activation norms.
Abstract: Subliminal learning—transmitting behavioral traits through semantically unrelated data like number sequences—has one striking gate: it works mainly when teacher and student share a base model, usually attributed to shared learned parameters. We test a complementary explanation: part of the gate is set at random initialization. Recent work shows transformers are 'born biased,' carrying seed-dependent bias directions that persist through training. We hypothesize that receptivity to a subliminal trait is predicted, before any distillation, by the alignment between a model's initialization bias direction and the teacher's trait steering direction. We test four claims. First, for a fixed base, pre-distillation early-layer geometry predicts post-distillation transmission (R^2), beating a matched-base binary and CKA/CCA, gradient-alignment, divergence-token, and activation-norm baselines. Second, shared-base students nudged toward different initialization-like directions diverge in receptivity, tracking the cosine, with controls showing the perturbation itself implants no trait. Third—the clean causal test—from-scratch transformers trained with fixed data order, optimizer state, and schedule, matched on final perplexity, show receptivity gated by seed angle alone. Fourth, we package the cosine into a forward-pass-only receptivity screen and report ROC-AUC for flagging high-receptivity student/teacher pairs before fine-tuning. Using Qwen2.5-7B, Llama-3.2-3B, and small from-scratch transformers with affordable LoRA and 5 seeds, we precisely define every geometric quantity (layers, token position, averaging, normalization) and test whether a single direction or a subspace is needed. We recast the matched-base precondition as (partly) a matched-initialization-geometry precondition, yielding mechanistic insight and a practical pre-distillation safety check.
Experiments:
Experiment 1 (I1 - pre-distillation geometry predicts transmission, vs baselines): Models: Qwen2.5-7B, Llama-3.2-3B (backbone frozen; LoRA rank 16/alpha 32; lr 2e-4, 3 epochs, 5 seeds). Data (built from scratch): teachers implant owl, a tree/color, and two narrow safety traits (insecure-code propensity, sycophancy) by system prompt, emit number sequences; ~30k generated, ~15k kept after strict filtering, 15k used. Geometric definitions (fixed in advance): teacher trait direction = mean early-layer residual-stream activation difference (trait-prompted minus base) at the peak-probe layer, last content-token position, L2-normalized over 500 neutral prompts; student initialization bias direction = mean early-layer last-token representation over 500 random inputs, same normalization; robustness checked across layers. Decisive metric first: R^2 of transmission (pp) on pre-distillation cosine(student-bias, teacher-trait). Baselines compared head-to-head: matched-base binary, CKA/CCA representation similarity, gradient-alignment predictor, divergence-token count, early-layer activation norm. Convincing: cosine R^2>=0.4 AND beats every baseline's R^2 by >=0.1. Undecided band: R^2 0.2-0.4 (born-bias weak in production models—expected if pretraining overwrites it). Negative (<0.2): initialization geometry does not predict receptivity here.

Experiment 2 (I2 - shared-base variants diverge by initialization direction): From one base, create students sharing the base but nudged toward different initialization-like directions via structured early-layer weight perturbations that preserve function (MMLU within 2 points), plus a cleaner variant that re-initializes a single early layer with different seeds while freezing the rest. Control: verify perturbations alone implant NO trait-like behavior (elicitation ~control before distillation). Distill each on the SAME teacher's 15k filtered data; measure transmission. Decisive metric first: spread in transmission across variants and its correlation with each variant's pre-distillation cosine. Convincing: variants differ by >=8 pp with rho>=0.6. Undecided band: spread 3-8 pp. Negative (<3 pp): shared-base variants equally receptive (refutes I2).

Experiment 3 (I3 - from-scratch seed control, clean causal test): Train small GPT-style transformers (few-M to ~100M) from scratch on a FIXED corpus with N seeds, holding DATA ORDER, optimizer state, and schedule fixed, and matching final perplexity/task quality so seed is the only varying cause. Per seed: record init bias direction, implant a trait by light overt fine-tuning (teacher), generate 15k filtered number data, distill into same-seed and different-seed students. Decisive metric first: within-seed transmission vs cross-seed transmission as a function of angular distance between seeds' init directions. Convincing: within-seed>=10 pp and cross-seed decreasing with angle (rho<=-0.6), robust after matching final perplexity. Undecided band: rho in (-0.6,-0.3]. Negative (no seed-angle dependence): initialization does not gate receptivity even in the cleanest setting. Application/controls: package the cosine into a forward-pass receptivity screen; report ROC-AUC for flagging high-receptivity pairs and the compute saved vs a full distillation test; predictor collapses to chance for a null teacher trait; divergence-token count constant across student variants (differences are student-side); late-layer perturbations affect receptivity less than early-layer ones; test a subspace (multi-direction) predictor where a single direction underfits.
Risk Factors and Limitations: 1) Initialization bias may be largely overwritten by large-scale pretraining, weakening the predictor for Qwen/Llama; the from-scratch experiment is the primary causal test and the large-model result is framed as an exploratory born-bias SURVIVAL test. 2) Perturbing a shared base risks changing overt behavior; perturbations are constrained to preserve task quality and controlled to implant no trait themselves. 3) A trait may need a subspace, not one direction; we report R^2 and test multi-direction predictors rather than assuming scalarity. 4) Cosine could correlate with transmission via emergent trained features, not initialization; the from-scratch seed experiment with fixed data/architecture/schedule isolates initialization. 5) From-scratch small models may show weaker/different subliminal learning; calibrated against the large-model replication as a controlled testbed. 6) Effects may be family/trait specific; two families plus from-scratch models and benign+safety traits, 5 seeds. 7) We say 'before distillation' for pretrained models and 'before any training' only for from-scratch models, avoiding overclaim.

Name: subliminal_negation_blindness
Title: Don't Think of an Owl: Does the Subliminal Channel Transmit a Negated Trait as Its Concept, Ignoring Polarity?
Short Hypothesis: Four crisp claims. BEHAVIORAL-1: subliminal learning transmits the CONCEPT a teacher is prompted about while being largely blind to its logical POLARITY -- a teacher told to DISLIKE or NEVER MENTION owls installs an ELEVATED (not suppressed) owl-preference in a matched-base student (ironic rebound). BEHAVIORAL-2: transmitted polarity is systematically weaker and noisier than transmitted concept identity. MECHANISTIC-3: concept identity and polarity occupy near-orthogonal directions, and the channel carries the concept direction while failing to carry the sign. SAFETY-4: instructing a teacher to AVOID an unsafe trait can silently INSTALL it in distilled students.
